Weather / Force Majeure Policy: If temples close mid-tour or roads are blocked due to landslides, government orders, cloudbursts, or any natural event, no cash refund is issued. A full rebooking credit valid for the remainder of the 2026 season (April–November) is provided. Kedarnath helicopter bookings are governed by IRCTC/UTT's own cancellation policy and are separate from this package.
Practical Tips

ATM Cash — Haridwar is the Last Reliable Stop: Moti Bazaar in Haridwar has 6–8 ATMs within walking distance of most hotels. Withdraw ₹8,000–₹12,000 per person for pony, palki, prasad, dhabas, and temple pujas. Beyond Joshimath, ATMs exist but frequently run out of cash or have connectivity issues.
Kedarnath Departure Timing is Non-Negotiable: The SDRF recommends trekkers leave Gaurikund no later than 2:00 PM and complete the descent before dark. Start from Gaurikund by 6:00 AM at the latest — our 4:30 AM Guptkashi departure ensures this. Late starters risk being stranded on the trail after dark.
Guptkashi Night is Altitude Medicine: The elevation gain from Guptkashi (1,319m) to Kedarnath (3,583m) is 2,264m in one day. The Guptkashi overnight is intentional acclimatization — do not skip it or request a schedule change that removes it. Altitude sickness begins when bodies skip acclimatization.
Pack Thermals for Every Dham, Including May: Nights at Kedarnath (3,583m) and Badrinath (3,133m) drop to 3°C–7°C even in May and June. Carry full thermal inner layers, a fleece mid-layer, a windproof outer jacket, and wool socks. Cotton clothing is dangerously inadequate at these altitudes after sunset.
Mobile Network Reality Beyond Haridwar: BSNL and Airtel have serviceable coverage at Kedarnath base camp and Badrinath town. Jio is unreliable beyond Sonprayag. Inform family that you may be unreachable for 2–3 days around the Kedarnath section specifically.
Sonprayag Vehicle Ban — Plan Accordingly: Private vehicles are permanently banned beyond Sonprayag by National Green Tribunal order. All pilgrims, regardless of package, take shared government-operated jeeps to Gaurikund (₹40–₹50 per seat). This cannot be bypassed — not for elderly pilgrims, not for premium tier travelers.
Registration RFID Tags — Keep Physical Copies: Checkposts at Janki Chatti (Yamunotri), Gangotri town entry, Sonprayag (Kedarnath), and Pandukeshwar (Badrinath) scan your registration. Digital display of the registration is accepted at most posts, but carry a printout as backup — mobile signals at checkposts can be weak.
Senior Citizen Medical Certificate — Get it Before Departure: The Char Dham Shrine Board mandates a medical fitness certificate for pilgrims above 60 at the Haridwar biometric camp. The certificate must be from a registered medical practitioner and dated within 30 days of the registration date. Getting this before leaving Kolkata avoids delays at the camp.
highlights: Har Ki Pauri Ganga Aarti, Haridwar — Attend the evening Aarti at the most sacred Ghat on the Ganga. Our team positions the group at the upper-tier viewing area — not the crowded lower steps — 30 minutes before the 6:45 PM ceremony begins.

Yamunotri Temple — Surya Kund ritual — Trek 6 km from Janki Chatti (2,650m) to the temple at 3,291m, or opt for pony/palki. Cook raw rice in the boiling Surya Kund hot spring (104°C) as prasad — a ritual specific to Yamunotri that no other Dham offers.

Gangotri on the Bhagirathi — Temple at 3,048m at the banks of the Bhagirathi, with views of the Himalayan glacier valley. Less footfall than Kedarnath; Darshan is unhurried. Our group reaches by 10:00 AM — well before the 2:00 PM midday closure.

Kedarnath Jyotirlinga — VIP queue coordination — Our ground coordinator pre-registers the group for priority entry at this Jyotirlinga. General queue wait time in peak season: 3–5 hours. With coordination: 45–90 minutes.

Kedarnath Abhishek at 5:00 AM — The early-morning abhishek on Day 9 is the most intimate darshan experience on the entire circuit — fewer than 200 people, direct view of the lingam. Most packages miss this because they do not overnight at Kedarnath.

Badrinath + Mana Village, last Indian village — After Badrinath darshan, walk 3 km to Mana — the last inhabited Indian village before the Tibet border. Visit Vyas Gufa (where the Mahabharata was dictated), Bhim Pul (natural rock bridge over the Saraswati), and the Saraswati River that vanishes into the earth.

Devprayag — Where the Ganga is Born — Stop at the confluence of the Alaknanda and Bhagirathi on Day 12. This is the precise geographical point where the river officially becomes the Ganga. Most groups drive past; we stop for 20 minutes.
Triveni Ghat Aarti, Rishikesh — Final evening aarti at Rishikesh's Triveni Ghat as the tour concludes — a spiritually complete ending to the circuit.

do-dham-yatra-by-helicopter.overview:
Badrinath and Kedarnath are highly sacred temples in Hinduism. If you're thinking of visiting these temples in a comfortable way, without the physical stresses, then book the Do Dham Yatra by Helicopter 2026. In this tour plan, our team will take care of your meals, ground transfers, VIP Darshan, helipad assistance, and more. Get in touch to know more about our custom plans! See More

The journey to Badrinath and Kedarnath by helicopter will begin from Sahastradhara Helipad in Dehradun. From here, you'll be taken to the Kedarnath Helipad first. After Darshan at Kedarnath, you fly to Badrinath Helipad. From there, it's a short walk to the Badrinath temple. Finally, you'll be taken back to the Sahastradhara Helipad in Dehradun, concluding your Do Dham journey.
Why Start the Do Dham Yatra by Helicopter?
Starting the Do Dham package by helicopter is the best option for time-saving ways to visit the Kedarnath and Badrnath temples. This option is helpful for visitors who want to complete this journey without any challenges due to long treks and mountainous road travel. 
Mainly a helicopter journey reduces time to complete the sacred pilgrimage within one day instead of several days by road. It is comfortable for elderly pilgrims, families as well as for those who have limited time and wish to take blessings of these holy shrines. With organized arrangements, priority darshan, and smooth transfers, the helicopter option ensures a safe, comfortable, and well-managed pilgrimage experience for devotees undertaking the Do Dham Yatra.

We also offer customised plans, where you can tweak the trip duration and even add sightseeing destinations. Multi-day options are available — overnight stay at Kedarnath or Badrinath can be arranged on request. Contact our team for customised itineraries.

Passenger Guidelines

Follow the instructions given by the pilot and ground staff.
Each flight carries 6 passengers and 1 crew.
Do not approach the helicopter from the rear.
Adhere to the baggage limit (maximum 5 kg).
Report your body weight correctly. The maximum weight limit for a person is 75–80 kg.
Keep 1–2 buffer days in your itinerary as flight delays are common due to bad weather.
Do not touch the helicopter parts. Always maintain a safe distance from helicopter rotors at all times.
Total payload capacity is 420 kg for 6 passengers (as per Terms & Conditions).
Children above 2 years of age are treated as full-fare adult passengers — no concession on ticket price or weight allowance.

Altitude & Health: What Helicopter Pilgrims Should Know
Kedarnath sits at 3,583 m and Badrinath at 3,100 m. Even by helicopter, you will be at these altitudes for 1–3 hours. Altitude sickness (AMS) is a real risk even for helicopter visitors.
Symptoms to watch: persistent headache, nausea, dizziness, breathlessness at rest, confusion. If any of these appear at the temple — inform our ground staff immediately. Do not ignore symptoms hoping they'll pass.

Not recommended above 3,000 m. Consult OB/GYN before booking.



Best Time to Visit
The best time to visit Badrinath and Kedarnath is in two windows: May–June and September–October. The weather in these windows is quite pleasant, and therefore, makes for a comfortable time to go on temple tours and even indulge in sightseeing in the nearby areas. 
Avoid going in the monsoon season (July–August) as the heavy rainfall makes the road slippery and accident-prone. Plus, there's an additional risk of landslides. Even for helicopter pilgrims, monsoon means frequent flight cancellations due to cloud cover and low visibility. May–June booking is recommended for first-time visitors. 
And in the winters (November–April), the temples remain closed, and Darshan is not possible. 
Do Dham Yatra Significance
The Do Dham Yatra holds great spiritual significance in Hinduism. It is believed that whoever completes this pilgrimage has their sins cleansed and moves towards moksha.
Spiritual Significance of Kedarnath

This is also one of the 12 Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva. 
This is the place where Pandavas sought the blessing of Lord Shiva for atonement of their sins accumulated during the Mahabharata war. 
Being located at a very high height, the Kedarnath Yatra is seen as a test of faith and endurance. 
Kedarnath also forms part of the Panch Kedar circuit — the five sacred abodes of Lord Shiva in Garhwal. The other four are Tungnath, Rudranath, Madhyamaheshwar, and Kalpeshwar. 

Spiritual Significance of Badrinath

Dedicated to Lord Vishnu, this temple is a part of both the Chhota and Bada Dham circuit. 
It's also one of the 108 Divya Desams. 
It's believed that thousands of years ago, Lord Vishnu meditated here. 
Badrinath is the most significant of the four Char Dhams and is traditionally the final stop of the Char Dham Yatra sequence. The Badrivishal idol here is a Shaligram (black stone) idol — one of the most ancient in all of India.

What to Do in Bad Weather
The content here is mostly practical and good. One addition needed — concrete rescue/refund protocol: 

If your flight is delayed, stay calm and don't panic.

Sahastradhara Helipad Dehradun
It is located in Dehradun and is the main operational base for helicopter flights headed towards Badrinath & Kedarnath. It is an important part of the Do Dham helicopter Yatra itinerary. 

This is the gateway hub for the Do Dham as well as Char Dham Yatra.
It is located close to Dehradun's Jolly Grant Airport, which is very well-connected to cities like Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore, and Kolkata. This makes Sahastradhara helipad an ideal point for starting the aerial journey.
It is located at lower altitude than Kedarnath and Badrinath, and therefore, offers much more reliable and safer takeoffs and landings.
It can handle large passenger traffic.
It is easily accessible from both the temple and the city centre.

Kedarnath Helipad

The helipad is located just 500–700 metres away from the temple.
You can reach the temple from the helipad by a short walk.
Passengers must go through security checks before boarding.
Pilgrims are required to follow DGCA guidelines.
There are 3 helipads serving Kedarnath — Phata (~12 km), Sirsi (~14 km), and Guptkashi (~30 km). The operator assigns the helipad based on slot availability. All three require a government shuttle to reach the Kedarnath helipad landing zone.

Badrinath Helipad
This is the official helipad for the Badrinath Yatra. This is one of the most widely used helipad in Do Dham Yatra and offers the pilgrims a fast & comfortable way to reach the temple. 

It's located just a short drive from the temple.
Security screening is mandatory at this helipad.
Passengers are required to strictly follow crew instructions for boarding and de-boarding.
Wheelchair assistance can also be arranged on request.

As you arrive at the Kochi Airport or railway station, you’ll be greeted by one of our representatives who will transfer you to your pre-booked hotel.
Relax for some time and then prepare yourself to visit the famous attractions of Cochin, including:
Jewish Synagogue:
The Jewish Synagogue is one of the most religious sites in South India. In the Commonwealth of Nations, it is the oldest synagogue.
Dutch Palace (Mattancherry Palace):
The Dutch Palace is the finest example of the Kerala architectural style. It is known for its spacious and long halls with its central courtyard.
St. Francis Church:
St. Francis Church is considered to be the first European Church in India that reflects the colonial past of the city.
Chinese Fishing Nets:
These are a type of fishing net that you will find along the harbor's mouth at Fort Kochi.
Have an overnight stay at your hotel in Kochi.

itinerary.title: Day 1: : Arrival and Welcome in Thrissur
itinerary.description:
You will be warmly welcomed by our representative at Cochin Airport/ Thrissur Railway Station, and then you will be taken to Kalady, which is the birthplace of Sri Adi Shankaracharya. It is in the place of Kalady that Adi Shankaracharya practiced miracles through his presence. He got the Vedas perfect and devoted his life to the preaching of the Vedic Dharma by founding four mutts at Puri, Sringeri, Dwaraka, and Joshimath. It was rediscovered in the late 19th century by the then Shankaracharya of Sringeri, and the following consecration of a temple to Sri Adi Shankara in 1910.
Visit Sringeri Mutt:- Sringeri Mutt was constructed at the same location where the house of Adi Sankara was located.
After check-in, later drive to Guruvayur. Take a spiritual tour to Thrissur and Guruvayur temples. Experience the Divine atmosphere of these ancient shrines, covered with complicated carvings and colorful murals.
Experience the magical rites and sacrifices, with worshipers coming together to receive blessings of the gods. The calm and the inner spiritual volatility of these temples is indeed a very rewarding experience.

itinerary.title: Day 2: Exploring Athirapally Falls and Departure
itinerary.description:
After having breakfast, gear up to visit Athirappilly Falls, commonly known as the Niagara of India. The waterfall falls 80 feet into a tranquil pond. The green fields and foggy mist cover it, forming a magical sight that is enjoyed by a large number of people. The loudness of the water, the vividness of the forest colors, and the cool mist are to be remembered.
To take the bus or train, or the airport, exit the building after making a visit.

itinerary.title: Day 1: HANOI ARRIVAL (NIL)
itinerary.description:
Once you arrive at the Hanoi airport, complete your immigration process and get your visa on arrival. Our driver will be waiting for you at the airport and will take you to your pre-booked hotel.
Once you reach the hotel, check in and freshen up. Then get ready for the capital city tour.
13:30
: You'll be picked up by our driver and then taken to the
Temple of Literature
. This is the first university of Vietnam and was established in the 11th century. Do click snaps of its courtyards and ancient gates.
15:15
: Now, visit the
Hoa Lo Prison Museum
(aka "Hanoi Hilton") which showcases Vietnam's struggle for independence. You'll be surprised to know that this museum was actually once a prison used to keep political prisoners.
16:15 - 16:30
: Later, you'll be taken back to your hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Day 2: HANOI - HALONG BAY
itinerary.description:
Savour a delicious breakfast in the morning.
08:00 - 08:30:
Now a bus will take you to the scenic countryside to
Tuan Chau Island
in Halong City. Our guide will also be there with you. We'll also take a refreshment break during the journey.
12:00:
Once you arrive at the Tuan Chau Harbor, our crew will give you a warm welcome aboard the cruise ship. A safety briefing will also be given to you.
Get ready for a 5-hour journey on this tour where you'll get to enjoy the breathtaking landscapes, full of islets and outcrops, named after their unique shapes!
Enjoy the authentic, delicious
Vietnamese lunch
on the boat while admiring the beautiful scenery.
13:45:
You'll arrive at the
Bo Hon archipelago
. Deboard the ship and go for exploring the
Surprising Cave
(aka Sung Sot Cave). It houses impressive stalagmites and stalactites that resemble sea creatures!
Now you can go kayaking or indulge in a
bamboo boat ride
in Luon Cave, and discover the beautiful lagoons.
Later, visit
Titop Island
. You can enjoy the sandy beaches here that lie adjacent to the limestone Mountains. You can also take a trek to the top, from where you can get panoramic views of the whole area!
16:30:
Return to your cruise ship, which will take you back to the Tuan Chau Harbour. During your journey back, indulge in sunbathing and music, and the natural scenery all around you.
18:00:
Disembark from the cruise ship and you'll be taken back to Hanoi via the new highway.
20:00:
You'll reach your hotel. Enjoy an overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Day 3: FLY TO DANANG - HOI AN
itinerary.description:
Relish a nice breakfast in the morning.
After this you'll be transferred to the airport to take a flight to
Danang
. Once you reach there, check into your hotel and relax for a while. In the afternoon, get ready to explore the beautiful Hoi An Town.
15:00:
This is a guided tour, and we'll arrange our guide to meet you at the hotel itself. Your
Hoi An City Tour
begins!
The very first place on the itinerary today is the
Hoi An Market
. Get lost in its colourful sights, sounds, and smells! This bustling market is a must-visit if you want to do some real Vietnam shopping.
Our guide will get you tickets to the
Hoi An Old Town
(included in your package). Explore here the
Phuc Kien Assembly Hall
. The vibrant Chinese architecture here will treat you with bright gates, dragon statues, and grand rooftops!
Also, see the well-preserved old houses, like
Phung Hung Ancient House
and
Tan Ky House
. These homes are here for over 200 years and have withstood centuries of weather and war! You can also learn about the lifestyle of merchants that used to live here.
Now, visit the
Japanese Bridge
, which is over 400 years old. This was originally constructed to connect the Japanese and Chinese communities who live on either side of the waters.
Also, take a detour to the handicraft shops of Hoi An. You can explore the artwork galleries here.
Lastly, in the evening, take a stroll on the
lantern-lit alleys
and enjoy a boat ride on the
Thu Bon River
. Tourists release the floating lanterns in the river to attract good luck. Do capture the reflections of the lantern-lit surroundings in the river.
Take a restful night of sleep in your hotel at Da Nang.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 4: Full-Day Ba Na Hills Excursion (40 km / 1 hr each way)
itinerary.description:
Start your day with a delicious breakfast in the morning.
Now, you'll be taken to the
Ba Na Hills
, which is famous for everything from picturesque mountain scenery to entertainment complexes!
Once you get there, take a scenic
cable car ride
and enjoy the breathtaking landscapes that lie along the way.
Also, take a walk across the iconic
Golden Bridge
, which is held by the giant hands! Also, visit the following:
French village with European-style buildings
Flower Garden
Amusement Park
Wax Museum
Later, enjoy a delicious lunch at the mountaintop restaurants, which serve a variety of Vietnamese and international cuisine.
Later in the evening, you'll be dropped off back at the hotel, where you can take rest for the night.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 5: Fly To Ho Chi Minh - Cu Chi Tunnel
itinerary.description:
Treat yourself to a nice breakfast in the morning.
After this, check out of the hotel. Our driver will transport you to the Da Nang airport, from where you'll take the flight to the
Ho Chi Minh City
.
Once you arrive there, relax for a while. You'll be taken to the
Cu Chi tunnel
in the afternoon (60 km ride). Along the way, you'll get to see rice paddy fields and lush greenery. Also, enjoy the ducks and water buffaloes that swim in the rivers.
By 12:45 PM, you'll reach the tunnels. Admire this underground system of tunnels that span across 220 km! Discover the hidden chambers here, try the wartime food that the soldiers ate, and learn how the Vietnamese soldiers lived in these tunnels during wartime.
You'll also have the opportunity to shoot the AK-47, one of the main guns used during the war. (Completely optional).
The tour will finish by 7:00 PM, and after that, you'll be taken back to your hotel for an overnight stay.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 6: Mekong Delta
itinerary.description:
Relish a nice breakfast in the morning at the hotel.
Around 8 - 8:30 am, your tour will begin. Get ready for a trip to
My Tho city
, which serves as a gateway to the Mekong Delta. Take the one-and-a-half-hour bus ride, taking in the lush's greenery all around you.
Now, take a
boat ride on the Mekong River
, enjoying the floating houses and fish farms along the way. Do not forget to capture these beautiful moments.
Once you're there, visit the
coconut candy workshops
and see how the coconut candy is made. Take this time to also visit the bee farms where you can taste the real honey!
You can also enjoy the
authentic Vietnamese folk music
(Đờn Ca Tài Tử), which is also recognised by the UNESCO.
After that, savour some delicious
Vietnamese traditional lunch
under a tree shade.
Now, visit the
Vinh Trang Pagoda
which is the largest pagoda in the delta.
The rest of the time is for leisure which you can utilise by discovering the region on your own.
In the evening, you'll be driven back to your hotel by our driver.
Enjoy an overnight stay at the hotel.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 7: DEPARTURE
itinerary.description:
Savour a hearty meal in the morning and check out of your hotel.
Now, our driver will drop you off at the airport from where you can take a flight back home.
This concludes your trip. Hope you have an amazing trip with us!

.

boat ride

08h00:
Our tour guide will pick you up right from your hotel. Now, you'll be taken to the Ba Na Hills.
09h00:
Enjoy the

Walk across the iconic

You'll be dropped off at your hotel. The rest of the day is free for you to enjoy as you please.

itinerary.title: Day 5: Da Nang departure (B) - No guide

itinerary.title: DAY 01- Hanoi Arrival - Early Check-In, Afternoon: Half Day City Tour (D)
itinerary.description:

In the afternoon, you will enjoy a sightseeing
tour of Vietnam
. First, you will get a fascinating glimpse of Vietnam's heritage and royal past at the Temple of Literature. Then you will head to Old Quarter to explore Train Street and shops, cafes, eateries and enjoy exciting Nightlife.
Sightseeing Outline
Temple of Literature-
It was built in 1076 and served as Vietnam's first university for 700 years. It was used to educate Vietnam's royalty, mandarins and members of the elite.
Witness the beautiful well-preserved gardens and grand architecture which will take your breath away.
Train Street-
It's a famous narrow railway street located in the Old Quarter of Hanoi.
Enjoy the thrill of trains passing by and sip an authentic Vietnamese coffee
Old Quarter-
Explore the beauty of centuries-old architecture, and rich cultural heritage and enjoy exciting nightlife.
This place has 36 narrow streets which were traditionally named after guilds or trade that were famous there such as silk, silver, bamboo, cotton.
Also visit some of the traditional shops to buy souvenirs.
End your day with a peaceful stroll and witness a beautiful contrast of Hanoi's historical roots and rise of modernity.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.description:
Early in the morning after breakfast, we will depart from Hanoi and visit Ninh Binh province. It is 2 hours from the South of the City.
Enjoy the Ninh Binh sightseeing Tour. First you will visit the ancient temples at Hoa Lư and then head to Tam Coc and enjoy a two-hour boat ride along the Ngo Dong River. Your next visit will be to the Bich Dong Pagoda complex.
Note-
Meals- Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner (Indian food)
Overnight Stay at Hanoi
Sightseeing Outline
Hoa Lư
Hoa Lư is one of
the best places to explore in Vietnam
. It's an ancient capital of Vietnam during the Dinh and Le dynasties (10th-11th century).
Witness the mesmerizing ancient temples of King Dinh Tien Hoang and King Le Dai Hanh and get good insights of the city's rich history.
Tam Coc
It's is also fondly known as 'Halong Bay on Land'
Board a traditional Sampan boat ride and enjoy a scenic 2 hours boat ride along the Ngo Dong River.
From the serene waters, you will come across many scenic places like limestone karst mountains, lush rice paddies, and three natural caves that give Tam Coc its name.
Bich Dong Pagoda
We will not miss this beautiful Bich Dong Pagoda Complex. It is built on a mountain side near Tam Coc.
See the three levels of Pagoda- Lower Pagoda, Middle Pagoda, and Upper Pagoda and the breathtaking views of nearby areas and countryside by climbing at the top.
After the day tour of the natural and historical places of Ninh Binh, we will return to Hanoi in the late afternoon or early evening. Overnight stay at Hanoi to rejuvenate your senses.

Chandi Devi Temple-
Situated at Neel Parvat, dedicated to goddess Chandi Devi. It is a siddha Peetha.
Mansa Devi Temple-
Situated at Bilwa Parvat, Mansa Devi Temple is dedicated to goddess Mansa. It is also known as Bilwa Tirth.
Harihar Ashram-

Bhuma Niketan-

It is famous for attractive idols of gods and goddesses adorned with jewellery. You will also witness beautiful glass work on the temple walls.
Vaishno Devi Temple-

Doodhadhari Temple-
The temple is a part of Doodhadhari Barfani Ashram. It is dedicated to Lord Rama, Devi Sita and Lord Hanuman.
Bharat Mata Mandir-

itinerary.title: Day 1: Delhi – Haridwar
itinerary.description:
Upon arriving at Delhi, your journey towards Haridwar will commence which will take 5 – 6 hours. Upon arriving in this holy town you will be immediately checked in to your allotted hotel. During late afternoon you will be guided to visit one of the most auspicious sites of panch tirth within Haridwar, Mansa Devi Mandir, which is set on top of Bilwa Parvat. After sundown, you will be taken for the evening Ganga Aarti at Har ki Pauri which is accompanied by the rhythmic chanting of prayers and mantras immersing the surroundings in deep devotion and spirituality.
You will be spending the night in Haridwar.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 2: Haridwar – Joshimath
itinerary.description:
Early in the morning, you will be driven to Joshimath which is a 9 – 10 hours journey (depending on the weather and terrain conditions). Upon arriving you will be duly checked into your allotted hotel which will serve as the base for your trek next day to Badrinath.
Pro Tip:
Make sure to keep your luggage as light as possible and wear woolen clothing since no matter what month, it will be extremely cold. You are also advised to wear sports shoes for a more comfortable journey towards the holy temple.

itinerary.title: Day 3: Joshimath – Badrinath
itinerary.description:
You will be made to proceed towards Badrinath Dham temple and upon arrival, you will be required to take a holy dip in the Tapt Kund located close to the main Dham mandir. Everyone is required to do so before entering the temple for darshan.
Later, after the completion of your darshan procedure you will be taken for an excursion of the nearby places like, Mana gaon (the last village of India located on the Indo-Tibetan border), Vyas Gufa (an ancient cave where sage Vyas is said to have composed the epic Mahabharata with Lord Ganesha’s help as a scribe), Charan Paduka (a rock containing the footprints of Lord Vishnu) and Bheem Pul constructed on top of Holy River Saraswati.
You will then be made to head back to your allotted hotel in Badrinath where you will be staying the night.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 4: Badrinath – Devprayag / Srinagar
itinerary.description:
After completing the visit to first dham of the auspicious circuit, you will be escorted to Devprayag by road, which takes 8 hours to reach. Devprayag is an extremely pious town since it is located on the confluence point of Rivers Bhagirathi and Alaknanda giving rise to River Ganga. Upon arriving at Devprayag / Srinagar you will be immediately checked into your hotel where you will be spending the night.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 5: Devprayag / Srinagar – Rishikesh – Delhi
itinerary.description: Your journey towards Delhi will commence by road in the morning, which is a 9 hours journey. On your way you will be stopping for darshan at Rishikesh (located 2.5 hours away from Devprayag). Finally, upon arriving at Delhi you will be checked in to your hotel and the evening time will be free for your leisure activities.

itinerary.title: Day 6: Delhi – Bhubaneshwar – Puri
itinerary.description:
Your eastern leg of the yatra will commence in the morning when you will be taken to Bhubaneshwar via flight. The duration of the flight is for 2 hours 30 mines.
Upon arrival at Bhubaneshwar, you will be escorted to Puri on a bus journey of 2 hours. Once you arrive there you will be checked in to your hotel right away where you will be spending the night.
In the evening you will head on for darshan at Jagannath temple (the 2nd dham in the char dham yatra of India). Here you will be made to be a part of the evening Aarti and your darshan of the holy deity will be complete.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 7: Puri – Konark – Bhubaneshwar
itinerary.description:
Your journey towards Bhubaneshwar will commence in the morning via Konark (home to the famous Sun temple). From Puri the sun temple is located at a distance of 1 hour.
This temple, dedicated to the sun god is a magnificent structure which was built in the 13th century. Available inside the temple is the holy mythological chariot of the sun god along with detailed architectural work.
You will then resume your journey towards Bhubaneshwar, where upon arrival you will be taken to Parashurameshvara Temple, which was built in 7th – 8th century CE (one of the oldest existing temple in the state) and is dedicated to Lord Shiva.
Your next destination will be the Lingaraj temple 9 and Mukteshwar temple – both of which represent magnificent architecture and immense spirituality which radiates from them.
Finally, after a temple tour of the city you will be checked in to your allotted hotel for spending the night.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 8: Bhubaneshwar – Madurai
itinerary.description:
Your southern leg of the Char Dham Yatra will commence today. You will be made to board the flight heading for Madurai in the morning.
Upon your arrival in Madurai, you will be taken to one of the most famous temples in South, Meenakshi Amman mandir, which is a colorful and vibrant holy place and is dedicated to a form of Goddess Parvati, Meenakshi.
After completing your darshan you will then be taken to a glorious 17th-century palace of Thirumalai Nayakkar, by King Thirumalai Nayak (king of the Nayak dynasty in Madurai). Located at a distance of 2 km from the Meenakshi temple this palace is an iconic representation of the grand architectural style.
Your day of sightseeing in Madurai will conclude when you will be escorted to your hotel for an overnight stay.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 9: Madurai – Rameshwaram
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, your journey towards the southern leg of the char dham yatra to Rameshwaram will commence.
Upon arriving at Rameshwaram you will be immediately checked in to your hotel after which your sightseeing and darshan of the city will kick start. Starting with a visit to Rameshwaram temple which is the char dham centre in South. After completing your darshan here you will be taken to different temples like, Ramjharoka Temple, Ramanathaswamy Temple and Kothandaramaswamy Temple. All these temples are considered to be extremely pious and holy.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 10: Rameshwaram – Madurai
itinerary.description:
Today you will be made to head back to Madurai which is a 4-hour road journey. Upon arriving at Madurai you will be checked in to your hotel where you will be spending the night.
Evening time is free for you to do your leisure activities, like strolling in the nearby marketplaces for souvenirs or trying the local South Indian cuisines.

itinerary.title: Day 11: Madurai – Rajkot / Jamnagar / Ahmadabad
itinerary.description:
Your 4th and final destination for this all India char dham yatra will commence in the morning, by taking a flight.
Once you arrive in Rajkot you will be duly checked in to your allotted hotel where you will be spending your night. During the evening time you can go on a kathiawadi food binge and buy some local souvenirs.
*your destination will depend on the flight availability.

itinerary.title: Day 12: Rajkot – Dwarka
itinerary.description:
From Rajkot, you will set out to the land of Lord Krishna, Dwarka, which is located at a distance of 4.5 hours. Upon your arrival in Dwarka you will be taken for a brief sightseeing tour of the city starting with a visit to Rukmini temple (dedicated to Lord Krishna’s wife), Bet Dwarka which is also known as Shankhodhar which is actually an inhabited island on the mouth of gulf of Kutch at a distance of 30 km from Dwarka.
Finally, you will be taken back to your hotel in Rajkot where you will enjoy the delicious local Gujarati cuisine
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 13: Dwarka – Porbandar – Somnath
itinerary.description:
Today you will be made to head on to Somnath, which will be a 6-hour road journey. En route the journey, you will be made to stop at Porbandar – birthplace of Mahatma Gandhi, where you will be made to visit Kirti Mandir and Sudama (Lord Krishna’s friend and devotee) mandir.
Finally, you will reach Somnath (the western cardinal point) which will be your final (4th) destination for the all India Char Dham Yatra. During the evening you will be made to attend the aarti which is soul enriching and an opportunity which should not missed. After an auspicious visit to this holy temple you will be made to head towards your allotted hotel in Somnath where you will be spending your night.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 14: Somnath – Rajkot
itinerary.description: From this holy centre you will be made to head towards Rajkot, which is a 4 – 5 hours long road journey. Upon arriving here you will be checked in to your hotel and the evening will be free for you to do your leisure activities.

itinerary.title: Day 15: Rajkot Departure
itinerary.description: Today your all India Char Dham Yatra journey will conclude by escorting you to your location of departure from where you will head on to your preferred destination.

After savoring the delicious dinner, spend the night at the hotel.Meals:Lunch & Dinner |Hotel:Soaltee Westend Premier or SimilarPlaces You’ll See

You will be able to see peaks like API, Saipal, and Nampha, as well as the eastern and southern faces of Kailash. Enjoy the majestic and awe-inspiring view of Lord Shiva's residence from the comfort of your seat. You'll head back to your hotel for lunch after Aerial Darshan. Afterward, you will begin your return journey to Lucknow, where the trip will conclude.Meals:Breakfast, LunchPlaces You’ll See

From your window seats, you have a view of the South and East faces of sacred Kailash. Other mountain ranges, such as Mt. Saipal and Nampha, as well as Mansarovar, will be visible. You will return to the Nepalgunj hotel for an overnight stay following the auspicious Darshan.Meals:Breakfast, Lunch & Dinner |Hotel:Soaltee Westend Premier or SimilarPlaces You’ll See

Also, visit the sacred banyan tree!After your Kainchi Dham visit, you can go on exploring the nearby sightseeing places, such asBhumiadhar Temple. Dedicated to Goddess Shakti, it’s famous for its calm energy and less crowded atmosphere.Later, you’ll be taken on a sightseeing tour of the ever-so-beautifulNainital. ExploreNaini Lakeand theNaina Devi Templehere, which is also one of the 51 Shakti Peethas.Now, go on a trip to a trio of scenic lakes –Bhimtal, Sattal, and Naukuchiatal. You can spot migratory birds here. You can also just sit here in its pure serene vibes!The last trip of the day will be made to the most famous market of Nainital, that isMall Road. Explore the myriad of shops here, selling everything from handicrafts to delicious food. We recommend trying the local Kumaoni dishes such as Bhatt ki Churkani and the spicy Aloo ke Gutke!End the day by going to your hotel in Nainital and getting a restful night of sleep.Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 3: Nainital - Delhi (315 km / 6-7 hrs)
itinerary.description: Have a delicious breakfast in the morning.Afterwards, depart from Nainital towards Delhi, as your tour concludes today. Don't forget to capture the beautiful sunrise views over the hills as you leave Nainital!Our driver will drop you off at the Delhi airport or railway station, as per your preference. Hope you have a fantastic trip!

itinerary.title: Day 1: Arrival in Guwahati - Museum & Brahmaputra Evening
itinerary.description: Upon arrival at Guwahati Airport or Railway Station, our representative will meet you outside the exit gate, holding a placard with your name. You will be transferred to your pre-booked hotel for check-in.Today's sightseeing includes theAssam State Museum, where you can explore therich culture, history, andtraditions of Assamthrough its impressivecollection of sculptures,paintings, andartefacts. Later, you can enjoy the sunset cruise on theBrahmaputra River(subject to operation, on direct payment basis). The golden-hour view of Guwahati from the river is genuinely memorable.Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Day 2: Kamakhya Darshan + Guwahati Sightseeing + Departure
itinerary.description: Start early. The best time to reachKamakhya Templeis before 8:00 AM on weekdays to avoid long queues. It is recommended to purchase a VIP Darshan Pass (₹501/- per person, paid directly at temple counter) to skip the general queue.Visit the holy Kamakhya Temple, located onNilachal Hill- one of the51 Shakti Peethasand the supremeYoni Peetha of India. The inner sanctum has no idol; devotees offer prayers at a natural stone fissure in a cave, continuously moist from an underground spring. The experience is raw, quiet, and deeply moving.You can also visit the temples close to Kamakhya on Nilachal Hill:Dhumavati TempleTripureswari TempleMaa Tara TempleMaa Kali TempleMaa Chhinnamasta TempleMaa Bagalamukhi TempleMaa Bhuvaneshwari TempleMaa Banadurga TempleAfter completing Darshan, proceed toUmananda Temple(~7 km from Kamakhya), located onPeacock Islandin the middle of the Brahmaputra. Access is by ferry. Also visit theNavagraha TempleonChitrasal Hill, dedicated to the nine planetary deities.If time permits, stroll through Fancy Bazaar for local shopping and snacks.You will then be dropped at Guwahati Railway Station or Airport for your onward journey.Important Notes:Inform us at least 1 day in advance if you wish to arrange a special puja or ritual at Kamakhya Temple.Kamakhya Temple remainsclosed during Ambubachi from 22 June to 25 Juneevery year.After reopening,Ambubachi Mela is held from 26 June to 3 July. The premises are extremely crowded during this period. Plan accordingly and book well in advance.VIP Darshan Pass (₹501/- per person) is NOT included in the package price and is paid directly at the temple.Umananda ferry charges andBrahmaputra cruisecharges are NOT included; payable directly.Navagraha Temple — missing from original itinerary, covered in competitors, addedExact Ambubachi dates confirmed (22-25 June closed, 26 June-3 July Mela) — per original notePlaces You’ll See

kashi-gaya-prayagraj-ayodhya-naimisharan.overview:
Kashi Gaya Prayagraj Ayodhya Naimisharanya tour takes you to places where India’s spiritual heritage and traditions are still alive. See More

Kashi also called Varanasi, is the first stop. This city has many temples, but the Kashi Vishwanath temple is the main attraction here. It is around 3000 years old and one of the 12 Jyotirlingas.
Here, you’ll visit many more amazing places listed in the itinerary. After that, you will go to Gaya and explore Sita Kund, the place where Goddess Sita used to bathe during her exile (Vanvas). The journey then moves to Prayagraj, a city famous for the Triveni Sangam, the meeting point of three holy rivers - Ganga, Yamuna and Saraswati.
These rivers are very important in Hinduism. Now the journey continues to Ayodhya, which welcomes you with the glow of thousands of Diyas and colourful lights. It is the birthplace of Lord Rama and you’ll love its rich culture. Next the final trip is Naimisharanya, a peaceful and beautiful place surrounded by nature.  Here, you can also visit the historic Pandav Kila, where they mediated. So plan your Kashi Gaya Prayagraj Ayodhya Naimisharanya package to explore more!
See Less

highlights: Explore Kashi (Varanasi) including Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Annapurna Temple and the Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat.
Visit Gaya to see Vishnupad Temple, Sita Kund and perform Pind Daan rituals for ancestors.
Travel to Prayagraj with Triveni Sangam, Prayagraj Fort, Bade Hanuman Mandir and sacred rivers for holy dips.
Spend time in Ayodhya and Naimisharanya, visiting Ram Janmabhoomi, Hanuman Garhi, Dashrath Mahal and enjoy at Pandav Kila surrounded by nature.

itinerary.title: Day 1: Arrival in Kashi
itinerary.description:
Welcome to Kashi! On arrival at Kashi Airport/ Railway Station, our
My Quick Trippers
representative will meet you and transfer you to your hotel for check-in and some rest. If you hire a guide, they will travel with the driver and help you during the journey.
After checking in, you’ll start exploring the sights of Kashi-
Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple
- A famous place where devotees come for salvation (moksha) and peace of mind.
Darshan at Annapurna Temple
- People pray here to the food Goddess for wealth and a life without hunger.
Visit to Vishalakshi Temple
- A peaceful Shakti Peeth temple, where the eyes of Goddess Sati fell.
Baba Kal Bhairav Temple
- Popular temple where devotees offer alcohol as Prasad to Kal Bhairav.
Evening:
Take a boat ride on the
Ganges
and explore Kashi’s old Ghats, and enjoy the city’s spiritual vibe (optional, extra cost). Later, attend the beautiful
Ganga Aarti
at
Dashashwamedh Ghat
, either from the Ghat or on a private boat. Spend a comfortable night at your hotel in
Kashi.
Note-
The Kashi Vishwanath Temple is open from
3 AM to 11 PM
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: DAY 2: Kashi – Bodhgaya (284 kms/ 5-6 hrs)
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, travel to
Bodh Gaya
and visit the
Mahabodhi Temple
, a very peaceful spot and holy site for Buddhists.
Later, go to the
Mahabodhi Tree
, where Lord Buddha meditated.
Next, visit
Muchalinda Lake
, a beautiful spot to take photos, then you will also see the 80-foot
Buddha Statue.
Next, visit
Wat Thai Temple, Japanese Temple, Bhutanese Temple, Metta Buddharam (White Buddha Statue),
and
Karma Temple,
each place with unique architecture.
After sightseeing, check into your hotel. Overnight stay at
Bodh Gaya.
Note-
The Mahabodhi Temple is open from
5 AM to 9 PM.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: DAY 3: Bodhgaya - Gaya - Kashi (255-260 km/ 5-5.5 hours)
itinerary.description:
Early in the morning, after breakfast go to
Gaya.
On arrival, explore
Vishnu Pad Mandir
where you can perform Pind Daan, a holy ritual to respect your ancestors (family members who have passed away).
Next, visit
Phalgu Nadi
, a holy river where pilgrims pray and perform rituals. After that, visit
Brahmani Ghat
and
Gayatri Ghat.
Then travel to the sacred Sita Kund, and finally see
Maa Sarva Mangla Gauri.
People believe that visiting this temple brings the blessings of Goddess Gauri, who can remove difficulties and bring luck.
Return to Kashi in the evening and enjoy a relaxing overnight stay at your hotel.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: DAY 4: Kashi – Sarnath (10 km / 15-20 minutes)
itinerary.description:
Start your day with a boat ride on the Ganges and see the Ghats like
Assi, Manikarnika,
and
Harishchandra.
You can also take a holy dip and optionally visit
Kashi Vishwanath Temple.
Later, return to the hotel for breakfast.
Start your day after breakfast by visiting Kashi’s well-known temples-
Sankat Mochan Hanuman
(located near Assi River, a great spot for sunset photos),
Durga Mandir, Tulsi Manas
(where Ramcharitmanas was written), and
New Vishwanath Temple.
Don’t miss a walk around the
BHU campus nearby.
In the afternoon, drive to
Sarnath,
the sacred site where Lord Buddha shared his first teachings. Explore
Dhamek Stupa
(best photo spot),
Chaukhandi Stupa,
various
Buddhist Temples
and the
Sarnath Archeological Museum.
Return to
Kashi
and check into your hotel for an overnight stay.
Note-
Sarnath Archaeological Museum is closed on Fridays.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: DAY 5: Kashi - Vindhyachal - Prayagraj (150 km approx. / 4.5-5 hours)
itinerary.description:
After breakfast drive to
Prayagraj.
Enroute visit
Vindhyachal Devi
for a Darshan at Shaktipeeth. Later visit
Sitamarhi
, the temple where Mother Sita went into the earth.
When you reach
Prayagraj,
travel to
Triveni Sangam,
where the Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati meet, and take a sacred dip there.
Enjoy a peaceful boat ride and experience a holy bath at the Sangam.
Next, visit
Bade Hanuman Mandir,
then go to
Akshayavat Temple
inside
Patalpuri Temple
at
Prayagraj Fort.
It is believed that Lord Ram, Lakshman, and Sita once rested under this holy tree.
Visit Prayagraj Fort, also called
Allahabad Fort,
built by Emperor Akbar in 1583 near the Sangam, and then see the holy
Alopi Devi Temple.
If time permits, visit
Lalita Devi Temple
and
Shri Nagvasuki Temple.
You can also explore
Anand Bhavan,
home of the Nehru family.
On arrival, check into the hotel. Overnight stay at
Prayagraj.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: DAY 6: Prayagraj - Ayodhya (166 km/ 5-6 hours)
itinerary.description:
Enjoy breakfast then continue your journey to
Ayodhya.
Visit
Ram Janmabhoomi Temple
a sacred place believed to be the birthplace of Lord Ram.
Go to
Hanuman Garhi Temple
located on a beautiful hill, which is perfect for photography.
Explore Kanak Bhavan Temple,
a beautiful temple with gold plated domes dedicated to Lord Ram and Sita.
In evening watch the
Saryu River Aarti
at
Naya Ghat,
a truly divine experience.
Note
- Ram Janmabhoomi Temple is open from
6:00 AM to 10:00 PM.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: DAY 7: Explore Ayodhya’s Culture and Spirituality
itinerary.description:
Early in the morning you can visit the
Saryu River.
Take a holy dip in the river or enjoy a peaceful boat ride if you wish (optional).
After that, visit
Nageshwarnath Temple,
which is one of the oldest temple in
Ayodhya,
dedicated to Lord Shiva. Then see
Ram ki Paidi,
and later return to
Ram Janmabhoomi Temple.
Next, visit
Dashrath Mahal
the palace of Lord Ram’s father, King Dashrath.
If time permits, you may explore
Valmiki Ramayana Bhawan
(famous for Ramayana paintings),
Treta Ke Thakur Temple
(where King Vikramaditya placed idols of Lord Ram, Goddess Sita, and Lakshman), and also go to
Tulsi Udyan.
Later, drive to Lucknow.
If time allows, enjoy an optional tour of
Bara Imambara, Rumi Darwaza, Residency Complex, Gomati Riverfront, Janeshwar Mishra Park,
and
Ambedkar Park.
On arrival, check into the hotel. Overnight stay in
Lucknow.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: DAY 8: Lucknow – Naimisharanya Sightseeing – Lucknow (180-190 km/ 6-7 hours)
itinerary.description:
After breakfast in the morning, drive to
Naimisharanya.
Once you reach, visit
Chakrateertha
first, (the spot where the Lord Brahma's chakra fell) then explore
Suth Gaddi, Vyas Gaddi
(best photo spot specially in sunrise), and
Manu Satrupa Tapsthali.
Later, explore other important sites such as
Hanuman Garhi, Panch Pandav Kila, Gomati River
(a beautiful riverside spot, perfect for evening walk),
Vishnu Temple, Dadhichi Kund,
and the
Lalita Devi Temple
(Shaktipeeth temple where Sati’s heart fell).
In the evening, drive back to Lucknow.
On arrival you will be dropped at the airport/railway station to take your flight/train for your home.
This
Kashi Gaya Prayagraj Ayodhya Naimisharanya trip plan
ends with unforgettable memories.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 2: Elephant and Jeep Safari in Kaziranga Park
itinerary.description:

itinerary.title: Day 3: Temple Visit and Departure
itinerary.description:
Treat yourself to a hearty breakfast.
Now, you’ll be driven to the

itinerary.title: Day 1: Dehradun - Kedarnath
itinerary.description: Departure from Sahastradhara Helipad, DehradunAt approximately 7:00 AM your charter helicopter departs from Sahastradhara Helipad, Dehradun. Reach the helipad early to avoid any delay - your NIT representative will be present to assist. On the way, you are treated to aerial views of the Mussoorie hills and Tehri Dam, with the Garhwal Himalayan ranges growing closer.Change of Shuttle at Phata / GuptkashiAt approximately 7:50 AM your helicopter arrives at Phata or Guptkashi. As per government regulations, all pilgrims transfer to a government-authorised shuttle helicopter here. This shuttle is the only aircraft permitted to land at the Kedarnath upper helipad. The shuttle flight takes 8-15 minutes depending on your base helipad. Waiting time at the changeover point is typically 10 minutes to 1 hour. Carry warm clothing - altitude at base helipads can be significantly cooler than Dehradun.Arrival at Kedarnath Dham ShrineYour shuttle deposits you at the Kedarnath upper helipad - just 500 metres from the main temple entrance. A 10-15 minute walk (or Pitthu/Palki ride) takes you to the shrine. Your VIP Darshan coupon, included in the Namaste India Trip package, gives you priority entry - saving 2-4 hours of general queue waiting. You have approximately 1.5 to 2 hours at the shrine for Darshan, pradakshina, and quiet time. Kedarnath sits at 3,583 metres - walk slowly, take breaks, and do not rush.Departure from Kedarnath DhamAt 11:00 AM, you depart from the upper Kedarnath helipad for the return shuttle to Phata or Guptkashi. Return boarding at Kedarnath helipad is on a first-come-first-served basis - be at the helipad by your designated departure time.Arrival at Sahastradhara Helipad, DehradunAfter the return shuttle to the base helipad, your NIT charter helicopter carries you back to Sahastradhara Helipad, Dehradun - arriving by approximately 12:00-12:30 PM. Our car drops you at your Dehradun hotel or to the airport/railway station, bringing your Kedarnath Yatra by helicopter to a close.Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 1: Arrival at Cochin
itinerary.description:
Your tour will start as you reach Cochin Airport/Railway Station.
After relaxing for some time, you will get ready to visit the famous destinations of Cochin, including St. Francis Church, Jewish Synagogue, and Fort Kochi.
Have an overnight stay at your hotel after the sightseeing tour.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 2: Cochin- Munnar (04 hrs/140 Km)
itinerary.description:
After a delicious breakfast, you will be transferred to Munnar, one of the most famous hill stations of Kerala.
Explore spice plantations, well-organized tea gardens, and lush green forests.
After arriving at Munnar, you will check in to your pre-booked hotel and spend the rest of the day as you like, exploring the picturesque surroundings.
Have an overnight stay at your hotel in Munnar.

itinerary.title: Day 3: Munnar Sightseeing
itinerary.description:
Today you will visit the famous sites of Munnar:
Echo Point:
Echo Point is the place where your voice echoes.
Kundala Lake:
It is a scenic tourist place. The area has Cherry Blossom trees, adding to this place’s beauty. It is one of the most famous spots for photography.
Rajamalai (Eravikulam National Park):
It houses a large population of Nilgiri Tahr. People often visit this site to see the Neelakurinji flowers, which bloom once every twelve years. It is spread over 92 square kilometers and houses a wide range of flora and fauna.
Have an overnight stay at your hotel in Munnar.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 04: Cochin - Thekkady (4 hrs/130 km)
itinerary.description:
After a delicious breakfast, you will head to Thekkady.
Once you have arrived at Thekkady, you will check into your pre-reserved hotel and relax for some time.
In the afternoon, you will embark on a sightseeing tour. You will visit the Periyar wildlife sanctuary. In 1978, this thick evergreen forest was declared a Tiger Reserve.
You can also enjoy various adventurous activities in Thekkady. You can visit pepper, cardamom, tea & coffee plantations and enjoy a boat cruise on the Periyar lake.
You will enjoy cultural programmes such as Kathakali & Kalarippayattu in the evening and visit the Spice market.
You will then return to your hotel and have an overnight stay.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 05: Thekkady - Alleppey
itinerary.description:
After a delicious breakfast, you will embark on a scenic drive to Alleppey, which is also known as Alappuzha.
Once you have arrived at Alleppey, you will check into the houseboat and enjoy the backwater life.
As you enjoy the cruise, you will witness the village area and canals. You will have dinner, breakfast, lunch, and evening tea at the houseboat.
After the tasty dinner, you will have an overnight stay at your houseboat.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 06: Alleppey - Kovalam (4 hrs/154 km)
itinerary.description:
Have a tasty breakfast in the morning, and then you will head to Kovalam.
If you have time on hand, you will visit Sri Padmanabha Temple in Trivandrum (which is considered to be the capital of Kerala).
Later on, you will embark on a drive to Kovalam, an internationally renowned beach that has three adjacent crescent beaches. It is considered to be the favourite of tourists for herbal massages, swimming, and relaxing on the beach.
Once you have arrived at Kovalam, you will check into your pre-booked hotel. You can spend the entire day relaxing at the beach.
You can enjoy various activities such as skiing, surfing, kayaking, and swimming.
You will have an overnight stay at your hotel in Kovalam.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 07: Kovalam - Kanyakumari (3 hrs/90 km)
itinerary.description:
Post breakfast, our driver will transfer you to Kanyakumari.
Once you have arrived at Kanyakumari, you will check in at your pre-booked hotel.
You will then visit Vivekananda Rock, where you will find a memorial that is dedicated to Swami Vivekananda.
From the tip of India, you can enjoy the sunset of Kanyakumari. Return to your hotel and have an overnight stay.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 08: Kanyakumari - Rameshwaram
itinerary.description:
Embark on a drive to Rameshwaram.
Rameshwaram is known for its spiritual and historic relevance.
As per the legend, this is believed to be the site where Lord Rama built a bridge to rescue his consort Sita from Ravana.
After arriving at Rameshwaram, you will check into your hotel, and later you will head to Agnitheertham, Ramjharoka Temple, and Ramanathaswamy Temple.
You will have an overnight stay in Rameshwaram.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 09: Rameshwaram - Full Day Sightseeing
itinerary.description:

madurai-rameshwaram-tour-package.overview:
The Madurai Rameshwaram tour is one of Tamil Nadu's most rewarding pilgrimage and sightseeing circuits. Four days. Two cities. And more sacred sites, living legends, and coastal beauty than most people expect.  See More

The journey starts in Madurai — home to the Meenakshi Amman Temple, one of India's grandest Dravidian temples with over 33,000 sculpted figures. From there you travel to Rameshwaram, the sacred island city where the Ramanathaswamy Temple — one of the 12 Jyotirlingas — stands at the edge of the sea. This is where Lord Rama himself is believed to have worshipped Lord Shiva before crossing to Lanka.
Apart from temple Darshan, you'll explore the iconic Pamban Bridge with its spectacular sea views, the haunting ruins of Dhanushkodi, and the birthplace of Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam. Thousands of pilgrims and families have trusted My Quick Trippers for a smooth, guided experience here — and we make sure you don't miss a single important stop.

About Madurai & Rameshwaram
Madurai — The Temple City
Madurai is one of India's oldest continuously inhabited cities, with a history stretching back over 2,500 years. It is the cultural capital of Tamil Nadu and the second largest city in the state. The city revolves around the Meenakshi Amman Temple at its literal centre — the city's streets were laid out in concentric squares around the temple.
For pilgrims, Madurai offers the Meenakshi Amman Temple, the Thiruparankundram Murugan Temple (one of Murugan's six sacred abodes), and the Koodal Azhagar Temple (one of the 108 Divya Desams). For those interested in history, the Thirumalai Nayakkar Palace and the Gandhi Museum add depth. And Madurai's food — particularly the Jigarthanda cold drink and the famous mutton biryani — is a destination in itself.
Rameshwaram — The Sacred Island
Rameshwaram is situated on Pamban Island in the Gulf of Mannar, connected to mainland Tamil Nadu by the Pamban Bridge. It is one of the holiest sites in Hinduism — a place where Lord Rama is believed to have worshipped Lord Shiva before crossing the sea to Lanka to rescue Goddess Sita.
The Ramanathaswamy Temple here is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas and part of the all-India Char Dham pilgrimage (the four dhams being Badrinath in the north, Dwarka in the west, Puri in the east, and Rameshwaram in the south). The temple's corridor is 1,212 metres long — the longest temple corridor in the world. The Theertham Snanam ritual, involving 22 sacred wells inside the temple, is unique to Rameshwaram and forms the spiritual centrepiece of the visit.

How to Reach Madurai
By Air
Madurai Airport (IATA: IXM) operates regular flights from Chennai, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Delhi, and Coimbatore. Most metro connections take 1.5–2 hours. The airport is 10 km from city centre — our driver will pick you up directly from the arrival gate.
By Train
Madurai Junction (Station Code: MDU) is a major railhead on the Southern Railway network. Excellent connections from Chennai (Vaigai Express, Pandian Express — 8–9 hrs), Bengaluru, Coimbatore, Trichy, and other major cities. This is the most convenient and budget-friendly option for most travellers.
By Road
Madurai is on NH-44 (the North-South corridor). Regular bus services from Chennai (460 km, 7–8 hrs), Coimbatore (220 km, 3.5 hrs), Trichy (140 km, 2.5 hrs), and Kanyakumari (244 km, 4 hrs). State government SETC buses and multiple private operators run overnight routes from Chennai and Bengaluru.
Travel Tips & Guidelines

Dress code: Strict at both Meenakshi Amman and Ramanathaswamy temples. Men: dhoti or full-length trousers (no shorts). Women: saree or salwar-kameez (no sleeveless, shoulders and knees covered). Dress codes are enforced at the entrance.
Theertham Snanam: Carry a change of clothes in your day bag — you get completely wet from bucket-poured water. It is not a light sprinkling. Allow 1.5–2 hours for all 22 wells.
Sphatik Linga Darshan: Happens only at 5:00 AM. Arriving in Rameshwaram on Day 1 evening is the only way to experience this. Do not skip it.
Photography: Restricted inside Ramanathaswamy Temple and Meenakshi Amman Temple. Camera fees apply at select spots. Check at the entrance before shooting.
Dhanushkodi access: Private vehicles are not allowed beyond the Dhanushkodi checkpost. The last 18 km to the island tip is sand — only beach jeeps (local, approx. ₹50–₹150 per person) cover this section.
Cash: Carry ₹2,000–₹3,000 in cash. Temple hundi, beach jeeps, and local prasad shops are cash-only. ATMs in Rameshwaram work but can run short during peak pilgrim season.
Early mornings: Ramanathaswamy Temple opens at 4:00 AM. Early darshan (4–7 AM) means shorter queues and a more peaceful experience. Afternoon queues can stretch to 2–3 hours during peak season.
Senior citizens: Wheelchairs are available inside both Meenakshi Amman and Ramanathaswamy temples. Inform us at booking if special assistance is needed.

maharashtra-jyotirlinga-yatra-package.overview:
This 3 Jyotirlinga Tour of Maharashtra is designed for pilgrims who want to visit three of Lord Shiva's most revered sacred shrines in a single, well-organised journey. You will be visiting Trimbakeshwar (Nashik), Grishneshwar (Aurangabad), and Bhimashankar (Sahyadri hills) — three of the twelve Jyotirlingas of India, all located within Maharashtra. Each shrine offers its own distinct spiritual significance, architecture, and setting. See More

In addition to the three Jyotirlingas, the tour includes a visit to Shirdi for Sai Baba Darshan and a cultural stop at the Ellora Caves — a UNESCO World Heritage Site with the iconic Kailash Temple. We handle all your travel logistics: AC transport, hotel stays, daily breakfast, and experienced drivers familiar with every route on this circuit. You focus on the Darshan; we take care of everything else.Departures from Mumbai. Customised pickups from Pune also available on request. Book now to confirm your dates.Temple & Travel GuidelinesDress code: Traditional attire recommended at all three Jyotirlinga temples. Men: dhoti or full-length trousers. Women: saree or salwar-kameez. Modest clothing ensures smooth entry — no shorts or sleeveless.Rudrabhishek at Trimbakeshwar: Requires advance booking. Cannot be done spontaneously on busy days. Timings: 7:00–8:30 AM. Charges are separate, payable at the temple — not included in the package.Mangal Aarti: Grishneshwar at 4:00 AM and Bhimashankar at 4:00 AM. Attending even one of these is highly recommended. The overnight stay at Ahmednagar (Day 2) makes the Grishneshwar 4 AM aarti possible.Ellora Caves closure: Ellora Caves are CLOSED every Tuesday. If Day 2 of your tour falls on a Tuesday, inform us at booking and we will plan accordingly.Bhimashankar ghat road: The approach to Bhimashankar involves a winding mountain ghat road. Motion sickness tablets recommended for those prone to ghat travel. Allow extra time on Day 3.Sawan / Shravan month: Trimbakeshwar and Bhimashankar see very heavy crowds during Shravan Mondays and the Kanwar Yatra period. Route diversions are possible. Book hotels 2–3 months in advance if travelling in this period.Photography: Restricted inside the main sanctum at all three Jyotirlinga temples. Outer courtyards and Ellora Caves allow photography. Confirm at entry.Cash: Carry ₹2,000–₹3,000 in cash. Prasad counters, puja shops, and Ellora Caves entry are cash-only at most counters. ATMs available in Nashik, Shirdi, and Aurangabad.About the 3 Jyotirlingas in Maharashtra1. Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga, NashikTrimbakeshwar is located 28 km from Nashik, at the foot of the Brahmagiri hills — the source of the sacred Godavari river. It is the only Jyotirlinga in India with the Trimbaka (three-faced) lingam, representing Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh. The temple is particularly known for Rudrabhishek, Tripindi Shraddha (ancestral peace rituals), and Kalsarpa Dosha Nivaran puja — pilgrims come specifically for these from across India.Jyotirlinga Number: 9th of 12Darshan Timings: 5:30 AM – 9:00 PMRudrabhishek: 7:00 AM – 8:30 AM (advance booking required)From Mumbai: 180 km | approx. 4 hrs2. Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga, AurangabadGrishneshwar is the 12th and last of the 12 Jyotirlingas, located near Ellora village — just 1 km from the Ellora Caves. The temple features beautifully sculpted red-stone architecture. The presiding deity here is Lord Grishneshwar (Ghushmeshwar) and the lingam is a Shivling situated in a sacred water tank. The temple is also notable for being one of the few where the deity's name means 'Lord of Compassion.'Jyotirlinga Number: 12th of 12 — the last in the sacred sequenceDarshan Timings: 5:30 AM – 9:30 PMMangal Aarti: 4:00 AM | Evening Aarti: 7:30 PMFrom Mumbai: 340 km | approx. 6 hrsNote: Ellora Caves (1 km away) are CLOSED every Tuesday.3. Bhimashankar Jyotirlinga, Pune DistrictBhimashankar is set in the Sahyadri hills, roughly 110 km from Pune and 240 km from Mumbai. At an altitude of approximately 3,250 feet, the temple sits inside the Bhimashankar Wildlife Sanctuary — home to the Indian Giant Squirrel, Maharashtra's state animal. The Bhima river originates here. The approach involves a scenic ghat road through dense forest. Of the three temples on this tour, Bhimashankar offers the most distinctive natural setting.Jyotirlinga Number: 6th of 12Darshan Timings: Morning: 4:30 AM – 3:15 PM | Evening: 4:00 PM – 9:30 PMMangal Aarti: 4:00 AM | Evening Aarti: 7:30 PMFrom Mumbai: 240 km | approx. 5 hrsNote: Heavy traffic and route diversions possible during Sawan (Shravan) month due to Kanwar Yatra pilgrim rush.Places CoveredPlaceLocationSignificanceTrimbakeshwar TempleNashik (28 km)9th Jyotirlinga; Trimbaka 3-faced lingam; Rudrabhishek; source of GodavariPanchavatiNashik cityRamkund; Sita Gufa; Kalaram Temple; Godavari riverfront — Ramayana connectionShirdiAhmednagar districtSai Baba Samadhi Mandir — one of India's most visited pilgrimage destinationsGrishneshwar TempleAurangabad (30 km)12th (last) Jyotirlinga; Mangal Aarti at 4 AM; unique water-tank lingamEllora CavesAurangabad (1 km)UNESCO World Heritage Site; 34 rock-cut caves; Kailash Temple (Cave 16)Shani ShingnapurAhmednagar districtOpen-air Shani shrine; village with no doors — unique in IndiaBhimashankar TemplePune district6th Jyotirlinga; Sahyadri hills; Wildlife Sanctuary; origin of Bhima riverBest Time to VisitSeasonMonthsConditionsBestOct — MarPleasant weather (15°C–28°C). mahavatar-babaji-cave-tour-from-chennai.overview:
Take a spiritual journey from Chennai to the sacred Mahavatar Babaji Cave,See More

in the tranquil hills of Kumaon, Uttarakhand. A sacred place for the soul seeking peace, where in 1861, Babaji taught Kriya Yoga to Lahiri Mahasaya. Your journey with us commences from Chennai, where you will embark on a flight or train journey to Delhi and later a picturesque drive to Kathgodam, followed by Dwarahat, the door to Babaji’s Cave. The best part of this spiritual trek is a 3 km moderate hike with an incredible view of the Himalayas, dense pine forest, and a short walk from Kukuchina village to the destination.You will come across religious places like Kainchi Dham, Jageshwar Temples, and Haidakhan Babaji Ashram en route. This is not a mere stroll, and is more of a blend of guided spirituality, strolling nature, and long spells of silent contemplation, which is a lifestyle. Regardless of whether you are going as an individual or a group, the trip will be a celestial blend of spiritual discovery, natural beauty, and cultural integration.Why Go to Mahavatar Babaji Cave in Dunagiri?Below are some major points that one can consider to plan this spiritual trip.Historical, Spiritual, or Cultural ValueGo to the holy cave where Mahavatar Babaji initiated Lahiri Mahasaya into Kriya Yoga in 1861 - a milestone in the history of modern-day spirituality.Birthplace of Kriya YogaIt is regarded as the birthplace of modern Kriya Yoga, the adoration of spiritual seekers and Yogis across the globe.Scenic Panoramic Trek of the HimalayasTrek along a classic 3 km moderate uphill route from Kukuchina through beautiful pine forests (1 hour for the average trekker).The Atmosphere and Spiritual MeditationMeditation and Yoga: It offers a serene and spiritual ambience that is ideal for meditation and yoga to experience inner peace and religiousness.Immersive Retreat ImmersionStay at Dunagiri Retreat, which offers rustic-elegant accommodations, vegan Ayurvedic Kumaoni food, and yoga & meditation halls--designed for deep self-work.Why Choose Our Mahavatar Babaji Cave Tour Package from Chennai?Professionally Operated Itinerary - We prepare properly designed holiday packages that explore the whole of your journey, starting with Chennai to Babaji Cave, in order to help you have a smooth and memorable voyage.Smooth Travel Services - Whether it is flights or train tickets or local transfers, or guided tours, we do everything to make sure that you can concentrate on your spiritual trip.Having Spiritual Guides - Our learned guides give us the information about the life of Mahavatar Babaji and the spiritual meaning of his holy cave.Convenient Stays - We organize safe, comfortable, and clean stays around the cave and on the path leading to it to make sure that the time spent there is stress-free.Customized Help - Single traveler, family, or group Traveler, we tailor the itinerary to meet your needs and preferences.Safety and Reliability- We take your safety seriously. We guarantee authentic transportation, professional drivers, and 24/7 assistance.Low Prices - Our prices are affordable and no expenses are hidden, which offers the best packages for your money.How to Reach Mahavatar Babaji Cave in Dunagiri?There are different ways to get to the Mahavatar Babaji Cave.By Flight:Take a flight from Chennai to Pantnagar airport (approximately 125 km away from Dwarahat).If someone wants to get to Dwarahat, they can take a taxi from the airport.By Road:The cave is close to Dwarahat, Almora, and visitors can reach there by taxi or bus either from Almora or Haldwani.Delhi or Nainital- Take the road to Almora and get a taxi or other local mode of transport to reach Dwarahat.By Train:Kathgodam (approximately 108 km) is the nearest railway station to Dwarahat.Go by taxi from Kathgodam to Dwarahat.Best time to visit Babaji CaveThe best months will be March to June and September to November when the weather is nice and the trek is not so dangerous. The monsoon season (July-August) is to be avoided because of slippery paths and risks of landslides. Winters (December-February) are relaxing and may be extremely cold, so layer up.Tips and Tricks for a Stress-free JourneyThe following are 7 practical suggestions and tips on how to plan a Dunagiri Babaji Cave spiritual tour so that it becomes a seamless, safe, and spiritually rejuvenating trip:Pre-Plan Your Travel Route:As the cave of Babaji is in the vicinity of Kukuchina village in Uttarakhand, there is no direct connectivity with Chennai. Hence, it is highly recommended to book your tickets, stay, and transport wisely.Pack Smart and Light:Essentials include:Ankle support trekking shoes.Large sweaters (even in summer, it is cold in the mornings and evenings).A small backpack for water, snacks, and first aid.Raincoat or poncho during or around the months of monsoons.A torchlight/headlamp is needed when intending to go out in the early morning or late evening.Book Accommodation Close to the Cave:You will find YSS Ashrams, guesthouses, and homestays in Stay at Dwarahat or Ranikhet.In order to have an even more interactive experience, request permission to spend the night in the Yogoda Satsanga Society Ashram in Dwarahat.As a travel freak, I highly recommend that one should book his/her stay in advance.So, why the wait? Check out our best Mahavatar Babaji Cave trekking packages from Chennai and book your spiritual journey now!See Less

itinerary.title: Day 1: Arrival at Indore
itinerary.description:

itinerary.title: Day 2: Indore – Omkareshwar – Ujjain
itinerary.description:
Post a tasty breakfast, you'll be picked up from your hotel.
You'll be taken to the airport, where you will meet our ground representative, who will inform you about all the helicopter boarding formalities.
You're advised to arrive at least two hours before the flight to the helipad so that you can complete all the boarding formalities on time.
After around 25 minutes of aerial journey, you will reach Omkareshwar Helipad.
About Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga
Omkareshwar Temple
is considered to be one of the holiest shrines in India and one of the
twelve revered Jyotirlingas
. The sacred temple is located on Mandhata Island, which is situated at the meeting point of the Kaveri and Narmada Rivers. The island is in the shape of the Hindu 'OM' symbol. On this island, there are many temples, and the actual Jyotirlinga is believed to be in the Mamleshwar temple. To facilitate travelers to have a fast and secure Darshan of Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga, PM Shri Heli Tourism Service was started by the MP Tourism Board, as reported by
NDTV
.
Once you have arrived at Omkareshwar, you will be transferred to Omkareshwar Temple.
At Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga, you'll have VIP Darshan of Sri Omkareshwar Mahadev.
After the divine Darshan, you will be taken back to the helipad.
After flying for around 40 minutes, you will reach the Ujjain helipad.
Once you have arrived at Ujjain, you will be transferred to your pre-booked hotel.
Then you will visit the famous attractions, including Harsiddhi Temple, Ram Ghat, and the local markets.
In the evening, you will return to your hotel and savor a tasty dinner.
Have an overnight stay at your hotel.

itinerary.title: Day 3: Bhasma Aarti and Return to Indore
itinerary.description:

Next, you'll attend the Bhasma Aarti, which happens daily at approximately 4:00 AM.
About Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga
Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga is one of the holiest places dedicated to Shiva in India. The temple is a Jyotirlinga and one of the holy abodes of Lord Shiva. It is located at Ujjain in the state of Madhya Pradesh. This sacred temple is located on the side of the river Shipra. The presiding deity of this temple is Shiva in the lingam form, and it is believed to be Swayambhu.
After the Darshan, you will head back to your hotel and have a luscious breakfast.
You will be transferred to Ujjain Helipad from where you will take your flight to Indore Helipad.
With this Omkareshwar Ujjain Helicopter Tour package will come to an end.

itinerary.description: Mathura- Vrindavan - Where Legends come to life in the playground of eternal loveFamous for - 'Mathura-Vrindavan', are places which are celebrated as the birthplace as well as the playground of Lord Krishna. These places have a magnetic effect on the pilgrims and devotees with their temples of age-old lore and spiritual atmosphere. We will start our Mathura Vrindavan tour from Delhi, our driver will come to pick you from your desired location in Delhi and then we will head to Vrindavan. Here’s what we will see-In the Morning:Prem Mandir:Take a first step on the path of spirituality by visiting Prem Mandir, a magnificent temple consecrated to Radha and Krishna. Discover the detailed marble sculptures depicting the mutual love between the gods and goddesses.Banke Bihari Temple:Finally, proceed to the esteemed Banke Bihari temple where you can have darshan and see the deity of Krishna, who is presenting himself in a child form.ISKCON Temple:Walk through the peacefulness of ISKCON temple which is very famous for both its lively setup and interesting spiritual programs.Midday:Mathura Lunch:Treat yourself to a scrumptious lunch at a nearby eatery in Mathura where you get to experience authentic North Indian cuisine and beverages.Afternoon:Shri Krishna Janmabhumi Temple:The Shri Krishna Janmabhumi Temple, regarded by many as his birthplace, is where you should go. Admire the temple architecture and take part in the afternoon puja.Evening:Vishram Ghat:Spend your last of the day at the serene Vishram Ghat, on the banks of the Yamuna River. Vishram means Rest. According to a legend, Lord Krishna made Vishram Ghat his resting place after defeating the demon king Kansa.After completing Vrindavan Mathura sightseeing tour, we will drop to your desired location and commence your return journey to Delhi.Places You’ll See

puri-konark-tour-packages.overview:
Odisha is known as the soul of India for good reason. A well-planned Bhubaneswar Puri Konark Tour Package lets you experience the state's most iconic destinations within a compact 70 km triangle — Puri, Konark Sun Temple, and Bhubaneswar. Puri is one of the four sacred Char Dhams, home to the Jagannath Temple and the world-famous Rath Yatra. Konark's Sun Temple, built in the 13th century, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the finest examples of Kalinga architecture. Bhubaneswar, with over 600 ancient temples, is the historic capital that started it all. See More

This Bhubaneswar Puri Konark trip covers all three cities in 4 days and 3 nights. Hotel stays, daily breakfast, private AC vehicle, airport pickup, and an English-speaking guide are included. You visit the Jagannath Temple, Konark Sun Temple, Chilika Lake, Khandagiri-Udayagiri Caves, Dhauli Stupa, and Pipli village — in a well-paced circuit that works for first-time visitors, families, and pilgrims alike. 
Rath Yatra 2026 falls on July 16. If you plan to visit around that date, book at least 8 weeks in advance — hotels across Puri fill up fast. The Jagannath Temple also closes for 14 days during Anavasara (after Snana Purnima, roughly June–July) when Darshan is not available. Our team flags these dates at the time of booking.

Rath Yatra — July 16, 2026: Lord Jagannath's chariot procession from the main temple to Gundicha Temple. The Jagannath Temple remains closed this day, but all visitors — including non-Hindus — can have darshan of the deities on the chariots. Puri hotels fill up 2–3 months ahead.
Bahuda Yatra (Return) — July 25, 2026: The chariots return and the Suna Besha ritual follows — deities adorned in gold.
Anavasara Closure — approx. mid-June to early July 2026: Temple closed for 14 days after Snana Purnima. Exact dates confirmed by our team at time of booking.
Konark Dance Festival — December 1–5, 2026: Classical dance performances at the open-air amphitheatre at Konark Sun Temple.

Konark Sun Temple Light & Sound Show 2026
The Konark Sun Temple hosts a nightly Light & Sound Show after regular visiting hours. The 40-minute show narrates the history of King Narasimhadeva I and the Sun God Surya through projected lights and audio. Wireless headphones are provided in Hindi, English, or Odia.
Timings:

March to November: 7:30 PM and 8:20 PM (two shows nightly)
December to February: 6:30 PM and 7:30 PM (two shows nightly)

Ticket Price: ₹30 per person (separate from temple entry ticket of ₹40)
Tickets are available at the Konark site entrance or online on the ASI e-ticketing portal. Online booking is recommended during peak season (October–February). This show is an optional add-on — not included in the package price. If you want to attend, let us know at the time of booking and we will adjust the Day 2 schedule to allow for it.
How to Reach Bhubaneswar
By Air Biju Patnaik International Airport, Bhubaneswar (IATA: BBI) is connected to Delhi (approx. 2 hours), Mumbai (2.5 hours), and Kolkata (1 hour). Puri is 60 km from the airport, around 1.5 hours by road. Our representative meets you at the terminal exit.
By Train Bhubaneswar Railway Station is on the Howrah–Chennai main line. Key trains from Delhi: Bhubaneswar Rajdhani (22–25 hours). From Kolkata: multiple express trains (5–6 hours). Puri Railway Station also receives direct trains from Kolkata and Delhi — pickup from both stations is available.
By Road Delhi to Bhubaneswar: approx. 1,750 km via NH44 (26–28 hours by overnight bus or self-drive). Kolkata to Bhubaneswar: 480 km via NH16, 7–8 hours. All transfers within this tour — Bhubaneswar to Konark (65 km), Konark to Puri (35 km) — are covered by the package vehicle.
