The Madurai Rameshwaram Kanyakumari tour package shows you temples, beaches, beautiful landscapes and rich South Indian culture. Journey begins in Madurai famous for its Meenakshi Amman Temple. An interesting fact about this temple is that it has around 33,000 carvings and statues covering every corner..
This temple’s architecture is truly unique - imagine how special it will feel when you visit there. The next stop is Rameshwaram. Here, the beaches look stunning and crystal clear. If you get time, don't forget to click sunset photos. You will also visit the popular Ramanathaswamy Temple, one of the 12 Jyotirlingas in India.
After visiting Rameshwaram, trip continues to Kanyakumari. Here, you can see the meeting point of three oceans- the Bay of Bengal, the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean, which creates unforgettable memories. You will also visit the Kumari Amman Temple, a sacred Shakti Peetha. According to legend, Sati Devi’s spine fell here while Lord Shiva carried her body. So get ready and experience the magic of South India on your Madurai Rameshwaram Kanyakumari trip.

Early in the morning, around
5:00 AM

also called

during

Bewitch yourself with spiritual practices performed at Har Ki Pauri Ghat and take part in the marvelous evening Aarti ceremony. Visit the landmarks of Rishikesh with an experienced guide and enjoy the serenity of Beetles Ashram for some leisure time. Enjoy the flavors of North India’s cuisine and rest in your comfortable lodgings each evening. Come with us for an uplifting soul trip at the intersection of spirituality and cultural immersion in the quiet background of theGanges River Valley.In the morning, leave Delhi by private car or bus and get to Haridwar.As you reach the town, head to the hotel for some refreshments before visitingHar Ki Pauri Ghat- the famous Ghat on the Ganges.Explore the scenic serene temples for spiritual nourishment. Some of the most popular temples of Haridwar areChandi Devi Temple, Mansa Devi Temple, and Maya Devi Templeetc.Be a part of the immersive evening`Aarti`ceremony performed by the Pujaris and get yourself involved in the divine aura.A walk at the markets nearHar Ki Pauriwhile shopping for traditional handicrafts and then having lunch is a pleasant way to relax.Return to the hotel for a night's comfortable stay and recollect your spiritual encounters from the day.Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 6: Departure from Guwahati
itinerary.description: You’ll be transferred to the Guwahati airport/railway station for your onward journey.

itinerary.title: Day 1: Dehradun – Devprayag – Rudraprayag – Guptkashi/Sitapur (200 km / 7 hrs)
itinerary.description: After your arrival in Dehradun, you’ll meet our representative at the airport/railway station. He’ll then assist you further.You’ll be then driven through scenic landscapes to Sitapur, where stops will be made at Devprayag and Rudraprayag so that you can enjoy the confluence of holy rivers at these locations.Then a visit to the Vishwanath Temple in Guptkashi is planned.After finishing sightseeing of the day, you’ll be checked into your pre-booked hotel. Now, enjoy a restful night’s sleep.Further Information:Rudraprayag: Confluence of the Mandakini and Alaknanda rivers, with attractions like Rudranath Temple and Narad Silla.Devprayag: Confluence of the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda rivers, and the nearby Raghunath Temple.

itinerary.title: Day 2: Kedarnath - Badrinath (Helicopter)
itinerary.description: Begin your day with a hearty breakfast! Then leave for the helipad.Here, you’ll get a safety briefing by the ground crew, regarding the do’s and don’ts during the helicopter trip.Next, you’ll be flown to Kedarnath and Badrinath. You’ll be given V.I.P. Darshan slips, so that you can skip queues and head straight for the Darshan.Complete your Darshan and Poojan at the shrines. After temple visits, explore local sights if there’s still time remaining.Now return to your hotel for a restful night.Note:Delays due to NOTAMs, weather, or other factors will be communicated in advance.Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 3: Sitapur/Phata – Rishikesh – Dehradun (200 km / 7 hrs)
itinerary.description: Today, we’ll drive back to Dehradun. We’ll also make a stop at Rishikesh to explore its various beautiful locations:• Ram Jhula and Laxman Jhula • Shivanand Ashram • Gita Bhavan • Parmarth NiketanYour journey concludes with a drop-off at Dehradun Airport or Railway Station. From here on, you can continue your journey towards home or other places.

itinerary.title: Day 1: Colombo Airport - Chilaw - Sigiriya
itinerary.description: Our representative will welcome you at Colombo Airport.We will travel to Sigiriya and stop at Chilaw to visit two important temples:Manavari Temple: This is where Lord Rama placed the first lingam, known as the Ramalinga Shiva.Munneswaram Temple: After killing Ravana in battle, Lord Rama prayed here to remove the curse of killing a Brahmin. Therefore, Lord Rama was advised to place four lingams to remove the curse.Next, continue your journey to Sigiriya.Check into the hotel. Enjoy dinner and stay overnight.Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 2: Sigiriya - Trincomalee - Sigiriya
itinerary.description: After breakfast at the hotel, visit Trincomalee to explore and learn about its important historical places and sacred sacred sites.Go to Shankar Devi Temple, a Shakti Peetam built by King Ravana. The original temple was destroyed, but the statue is now worshiped in a nearby temple.Visit Thirukoneswaram Temple, constructed by Rishi Agastya as per Lord Shiva’s guidance. This temple is also filled with interesting history.Now, proceed to Kanniya Hot Wells, where it is believed that Ravan’s trishul (trident) created seven hot water springs during his mother’s funeral.After visiting Trincomalee’s sacred places, return to Sigiriya for a relaxing evening. Then, stay overnight at your hotel and have dinner.Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 3: Sigiriya - Kandy
itinerary.description: After breakfast, move towards the Sigiriya Rock Fortress, an important historical site in Sri Lanka.Sigiriya is called the ’Eighth Wonder of the World’ and is popular for its palace.The rock fortress is a part of the Ramayana and it is connected to the story of Ravana and SIta.In Sigiriya, visitors can see the Cobra Hooded Cave has ancient drawings where Ravana kept Sita.On the way to Kandy, visit an Ayurveda and Herbal Garden, popular for its healing benefits and it is connected to the story of Hanuman.After your visit, check into your hotel in Kandy for a night stay.Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 4: Kandy
itinerary.description: Have your breakfast, and visit Sita Kotuwa, known as the spot where Ravana kept Sita captive.Sita Kotuwa is a beautiful place surrounded by waterfalls and greenery, which is connected to the stories of the Ramayana.In the afternoon, go back to Kandy to explore Sri Dalada Maligawa, a popular UNESCO spot with Buddha’s holy tooth relic.In the evening, enjoy a dance event and thrilling fire-walking.Stay overnight in Kandy and have dinner.Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 5: Kandy - Nuwara Eliya
itinerary.description: After breakfast, begin your day with the Kandy trip, where you can enjoy the beautiful views, green landscapes and visit craft centers.On the way, travel to Nuwara Eliya and enjoy the scenic views.Visit the Tea Gardens to see Sri Lanka’s popular tea plantations, learn the tea-making process, and taste fresh Ceylon tea.Now, stop at Sri Baktha Hanuman Temple, dedicated to Lord Hanuman. It is believed that this is the place where he searched for Sita.Next, enjoy Ramboda Falls, one of the tallest and beautiful waterfalls in Sri Lanka.When you reach Nuwara Eliya, check into the hotel, enjoy dinner and stay overnight.Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 6: Nuwara Eliya - Ella Kataragama
itinerary.description: Go to Gayathri Peedam, where it is believed that Ravan’s son Meghanath got magical powers from Lord Shiva.Travel to Amma Temple, the believed site of Sita’s captivity, you can see the river where she prayed and the rocks with Hanuman’s footprints. You can also visit Hakgala Botanical Gardens.Go to Divurumpola, the place where Sita proved her purity through Agni Pariksha.Visit Ella, a village connected to Ramayana history, and explore Ravana Ella Cave and Ravana Falls, where Sita used to bathe in a pool.Explore Kataragama Temple, dedicated to Lord Karthikeya Subramaniam, who protected Rama in the battle to defeat Ravana.Stay overnight and enjoy dinner.Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 7: Kataragama - Galle - Colombo
itinerary.description: Next day, start the morning with a Pooja at Kataragama Temple, then enjoy breakfast.Travel to Colombo in two famous places- Rumassala Mountain, where it is believed that Lord Hanuman dropped part of the Sanjeevani Mountain, popular for its healing benefits.Now, visit Panchamuga Anjaneyar Temple in Sri Lanka, there is a chariot dedicated to Lord Hanuman, and an annual chariot festival is also celebrated here.Next proceed to Kelaniya Temple, where Vibhishana was made King of Lanka. The temple has paintings of his crowning and a statue dedicated to him.Stay overnight in Colombo and have dinner.Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 8: Colombo - Airport Departure
itinerary.description: In the morning, enjoy breakfast and say goodbye to the Ramayana trip.Go to Colombo International Airport, taking unforgettable memories and photos of your journey.

Include the following sites in your itinerary to see it all and have a full-fledged journey:PlaceDescription / SignificanceSeetha Amman Temple (Nuwara Eliya)According to the Ramayana, this is the place where Goddess Sita was held captive by Ravana. This temple houses Ashok Vatika where Sita spent her days in captivity. The temple also possesses a beautiful Sita idol.Ravana Falls (Kandy)This majestic waterfall is widely believed to be the place where Ravana used to take his baths. It beautifully cascades down in a number of tiers and makes for a perfect tourist spectacle. It must be included in your Sri Lanka Ramayana holiday package.Hakgala Botanical GardenThis place lies in close proximity to Ashoka Vatika. This legendary garden has a variety of plants. Tourists just love to stroll around here and reflect on the Ramayana.Manavari Temple (Anuradhapura)According to legend, Manavari is the first place where Lord Rama set foot on after coming to Sri Lanka. It is also believed to be the place where he built a shrine and performed puja of Lord Shiva after defeating Ravana.Ramboda Falls (Ramboda)This is another waterfall that is linked to Ravana. Ramboda Falls is one of the places where he had his Pushpak Viman fly over when he was taking Sita home. He did this to show her the beauty of his kingdom. Today, travellers love the cold winds blowing here and enjoy the picturesque views of lush tea plantations surrounding the area.SigiriyaSigiriya is also closely related to the Ramayana. This UNESCO World Heritage site is a rock fortress where Sita was kept as a captive by Ravana in his kingdom. Tourists love the panoramic views from the top of the rock. A must-addition to the luxury Ramayana Tour Package Sri Lanka!Divurumpola (Near Nuwara Eliya)This sacred place is where Sita underwent Agni Pariksha to prove her innocence after her rescue. Therefore Sri Lanka Ramayana Yatra by air is the primary route to reach here.By Air (International Flights)Sri Lanka has a number of international airports. The two main ones are:1. Bandaranaike International Airport, Colombo:This is the primary airport in Sri Lanka for all international flights. It is approximately 35 km from the capital. The majority of international flights to Sri Lanka arrive here. The airport is well-connected to Asia, Europe, the Middle East, and other continents.2. Mattala Rajapaksa International Airport, Hambantota:This airport also operates international flights. However, it is less busy than Bandaranaike International Airport. It handles flights mainly from the Middle East and some regional destinations.Things to Do on the Sri Lanka Ramayana TourHere are a few things that you must do to make the most out of your trip:Explore Iconic Ramayana SitesRavana Cave: This cave is considered to be the place where Ravana hid Sita.Ashok Vatika: Now a garden, this place was once a prison for Sita.Divurumpola: This site is where she went through the Agni Pariksha.Visit TemplesSeetha Amman Temple: Sita was believed to have spent her time in captivity here.Koneswaram Temple: Legend says Ravana used to come to worship Lord Shiva in this temple during his rule.Sita Eliya Temple: This temple is built around yet another location where Sita was kept captive. A must-do activity on your Ramayana Yatra to Lanka from India! Talking about food, there are delicious Sri Lankan dishes that you can gorge on, such as sweet coconut pancakes, rice noodles, Kaju Curry, etc.Marvel at Natural WondersSri Lanka is home to one of the most iconic natural attractions. While you're there, do visit the Little Adam's Peak and Ella Rock and Sigiriya Rock Fortress. Also, visit the Ram Setu Connection. Although it's mainly on the Indian side, it's still a site to behold from the Sri Lankan shores!Explore Ancient CitiesAnuradhapura and Polonnaruwa are the two ancient capitals that have a plethora of ruins deeply connected to Sri Lanka's mythology.Tips for TravellersHere are some travel tips for your Sri Lanka Ramayana Circuit Tour:While you're planning for the trip, do check the visa requirements for Sri Lanka for Indian tourists.When you're visiting the temples in the country, wear modest clothes. Walk the very lands that once lord Rama and Goddess Sita set foot on! Book My Quick Trippers's Ramayana Tour Packages from India now and enjoy a comfortable trip here. Visit to the healing 7 wells.

itinerary.title: Day 1: Arrival in Sri Lanka - Chilaw - Anuradhapura
itinerary.description:
Upon arrival, you will be assisted by our tour representative who will make you head towards Anuradhapura via Chilaw. Upon arriving at Chilaw your Ramayana tour will kick start with a visit to Manavari Temple - the spot where Lord Rama had forst established a lingam after killing Ravana. This is an extremely sacred place since there are only two Ramalingam (lingams established by Lord Rama) in the world, one of them being in Rameshwaram. You will then be taken to Munneswaram Temple - this is the exact place where Lord Rama had prayed to Lord Shiva after committing Brahmahasti (priest killing).
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 2: Anuradhapura - Trincomalee
itinerary.description:
Early in the morning you will be made to proceed for Trincomalee but first you will be made to take a brief tour of Anuradhapura starting with a visit to Kanniya hot water spring well - a collection of 7 wells which is believed to possess natural healing powers and the place where king Ravana is believed to have carried out the last rites for his mother.
After covering a 2 hours road journey and upon arriving at Trincomalee you will be taken to visit the famous Koneswaram Hindu temple - which was built by Rishi Agastya after getting instructions from Lord Shiva who was highly impressed by King Ravana’s devotion. The temple is extremely unique since it is a temple which was built by the lord for his devotee. You will be duly checked in to your hotel for spending the night.
Your evening will end on a relaxing note at Nilaveli Beach where you will also witness the majestic sunset.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 3: Trincomalee - Kandy
itinerary.description:
Early in the morning you will start off your journey towards Kandy, while stopping on your way for visits to some of the most mesmerizing tourist attractions like - Sigiriya rock fortress - a UNESCO world heritage site, and popularly dubbed as the 8th wonder of the world is a triple moated defense from where a massive rock emerges to a height of 600 feet, which is complete with gardens and swimming pools on the summit.
You will then head on to Cobra cave - named so because of its shape and the place where Sita was held in captivity whose walls are covered in prehistoric inscriptions and artworks.
Upon arriving at Kandy which is located at a distance of 4 hours and 5 mines you will be checked in to your hotel, after which you will be made to attend the local and traditional Kandy dance show presentation.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 4: Kandy - Nuwara Eliya
itinerary.description:
Early in the morning, you will be taken on a local sightseeing of Kandy, where you will be made to visit the famous temple of the tooth - a sacred 16th-century site for Sri Lankan Buddhists which houses Lord Buddha’s tooth relic.
You will then be escorted to Shri Bhakta Hanuman Temple - where Lord Hanuman wandered looking for Sita and is visited by numerous devotees throughout the year.
Ramboda waterfalls will be your next destination - which is one of the most pristine and picturesque cascading
waterfalls in Sri Lanka
.
The island country of Sri Lanka is popular all over the world for its high-quality tea; you will be taken for a visit to the tea factory and tea plantation estates. Here you will also have the option of buying yourself some locally produced tea.
Your next destination for the day will be upon your arrival at Nuwara Eliya, Seetha Amman temple - a modern vibrant and attractive building which is dedicated to Lord Rama and Sita and enshrines both their statues.
Finally, you will be taken to the colorful and lively Ashok Vatika - the place where Sita preferred to stay in captivity under the Ashoka tree, hence the name.
You will then be duly checked in to your hotel after a wholesome sightseeing tour, where you will be staying overnight.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 5: Nuwara Eliya - Kataragama
itinerary.description:
Your early morning visit will be on an extremely colorful not, where you will be made to visit Hakgala botanical garden - one of the
5 most popular botanical gardens in Sri Lanka
and was Ravana’s favorite places where he kept a very depressed Sita.
Gayathri Amman temple at Nuwara Eliya will be your next destination - which houses numerous Swayambhu (self-created lingams). Next, you will be taken to the historic site of Divurumpola Temple - the spot where Sita had performed her Agnipariksha to prove her purity and took her oaths. Several years later the villagers still pledge their fidelity or take oaths.
Dhowa rock temple will be your next stop - it holds immense relevance since during the 1st century BC this place had served as the refuge place for King Walagamba. It also holds Buddhist importance since there is also a small stupa present inside the cave.
The small mountain hamlet of Ella will be your next destination which possesses this was also one of the places where Ravana was hiding Sita. The Ella cave is located at the massive Ella waterfalls (1080 feet). After exploring this glorious site you will be made to head on to Kataragama which is located at a distance of 4 hours where you will be checked in to your allotted hotel for the night.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 6: Kataragama - Colombo
itinerary.description:
You will be made to visit the famous Kataragama Hindu temple in the morning - the place where Lord Kartikeya had requested to proceed to the battlefield by Lord Indra during the last day of war.
Later you will be made to proceed towards Ussangoda - the place which was one of the burnt up areas caused by Lord Hanuman’s blazing tail when he was testing the might of Ravana. Galle fortress will be your next destination which was built by the Portuguese in 1588 which till present day reminds the visitors of the colonial past.
After covering a road journey of 5 hours you will reach the magnificent city of Colombo - the largest city of Sri Lanka where upon arrival you will be checked in to your hotel for an overnight stay.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 7: Colombo Sightseeing
itinerary.description:
Early in the morning, you will be taken on a fun riverboat safari on Bentota Madu. You will also be taken to the famous turtle farms.
Your sacred temple tour of the day will kick start with Panchamuga Anjaneyar Temple - the only temple on the island which is dedicated to the Panchamuga form (five faces) of Lord Hanuman. You will also be made to visit Kelaniya Raja Maha Vihara - a Buddhist sanctuary which is said to be visited by Lord Buddha himself. There is also a Hindu shrine present within the sanctuary.
Depending on the availability you will also be taken on a city-wide tour of Colombo which will cover the Independence Memorial Hall, old parliament and Galle face garden.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 8: Colombo Departure
itinerary.description: From Colombo, you will be made to head on to the airport which is a 1-hour journey where you will be made to board the flight heading towards your onward destination.

Srisailam Dam
Bhramaramba Devi Temple

Hatkeshwar Temple

Enjoy the amazing view of the Krishna River between hills. Its shape is like an octopus (a great photography spot)
Chenchu Lakshmi Tribal Museum
Paathala Ganga-
Many visitors come to Pathala Ganga for boating and to see its caves. It’s a great spot for nature lovers.
Ropeway, Srisailam
After you arrive, check in at the hotel. In the evening, visit the holy
Mallikarjuna Jyotirlinga Temple
located on the Nallamala Hills. Enjoy your night’s stay at Srisailam.
Note-
Mallikarjuna Temple is open from
4:30 AM to 3:00 PM
and
6:00 PM to 9:00 PM
.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 2- Srisailam - Hyderabad (214 Kms / 4-5 Hours Drive)
itinerary.description:
Start your day with prayer at
Lord Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple
.
Then explore
Sri Bhramaramba Ammavari Shakti Peeth Temple
, where Goddess Sati’s neck is believed to have fallen.
Now go to
Paladhara-Panchadhara
, a very beautiful spot surrounded by nature. If you get a chance, try camping as well.
Climb
Sikharam Hill
to visit
Shikaresvara Temple
, then proceed to
Sakshi Ganapathi Temple
and
Pathala Ganga
, and don’t forget to take a boat ride on
Krishna River
.
Later, drive back to
Hyderabad
. If time permits visit the
Statue of Equality
near
Hyderabad Airport
.
Spend a comfortable overnight stay in
Hyderabad
.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 3- Hyderabad Sightseeing
itinerary.description:
Start your day with breakfast and then explore
Ramoji Film City
.
Ramoji Film City
is one of the world’s biggest and most famous film studios, listed in the Guinness World Records.
Enjoy a day full of entertainment, shows, and sightseeing.
Return to the hotel for an overnight stay in Hyderabad.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 4- Hyderabad Sightseeing - Departure
itinerary.description:
After breakfast check out from the hotel and go for sightseeing. The places you visit today will depend on your departure time (optional).
Start your day at the historic
Golconda Fort
. Try clapping at the entrance - the echo travels nearly a kilometer. In the past, it helped warn soldiers during attacks.
Now proceed to
Nehru Zoological Park
.
Then, explore the famous
Salar Jung Museum
.
Next, go to
Chowmahalla Palace
, a beautiful place that took around 100 years to build. Its stunning design will surely impress you.
Later, visit
Charminar
. Try to visit in the evening if possible; the colorful lights make it look truly beautiful.
In the evening, visit
Laad Bazaar
, famous for its bangles, pearls, and traditional Hyderabad items.
Drive through
Hussain Sagar Lake
and
Lumbini Park
if time allows.
After sightseeing, you’ll be dropped at
Hyderabad
Airport or Railway Station for your next journey.
Your Srisailam Mallikarjuna travel package ends with happy memories!
Note -
Hyderabad city sightseeing
is not available on Fridays as many places remain closed.
Places You’ll See

highlights: Seek blessings at Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple, one of the 12 revered Jyotirlingas
Darshan at Sri Bhramaramba Ammavari Temple, one of the Shakti Peethas
Scenic views of Srisailam Dam
Enjoy photography at the Octopus View Point
Cultural visit to the Chenchu Lakshmi Tribal Museum
Enjoy a ropeway ride to Pathala Ganga
Experience boating on the River Krishna
Visit to sacred spots like Paladhara Panchadara, Sikharam Temple, and Sakshi Ganapathi Temple
Optional visit to the Statue of Equality near Hyderabad
See More

itinerary.title: Day 1: : Arrival in Hyderabad – Sightseeing
itinerary.description:
Welcome to Hyderabad! Our tour representative will greet you with a warm welcome once you arrive at the Hyderabad airport/railway station.
Now, you’ll be comfortably driven to Srisailam (a 4 hour long drive) in your private vehicle. Along the way, we'll stop at the following sightseeing places:
Srisailam Dam
- Take a picture of the breathtaking, massive reservoir
Octopus View Point
- Watch as the Krishna river meanders through the hills and in the process, makes the shape of an octopus
Chenchu Lakshmi Tribal Museum
- Discover the lifestyle of the people who lived in the Nallamala forests for centuries
Ropeway
- Take this ropeway to capture click bird-eye view shots of the Krishna River
Evening darshan of Lord Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple and Sri Bhramaramba Ammavari Shakti Peeth Temple.
By evening, you’ll be dropped off at your pre-booked hotel. Take a restful night’s sleep.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 2: Temple Visit – Srisailam Sightseeing – Departure from Hyderabad
itinerary.description:
Wake up early in the morning, and proceed to the Darshan of Lord Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple. After the close up with the divine, head to Sri Bhramaramba Ammavari Shakti Peeth Temple, which is housed in the same complex.
Now, we’ll take you on a sightseeing tour at:
Paladhara and Panchadhara Waterfalls
Sikharam / Shikaresvara Temple
Sakshi Ganapathi Temple
Patala Ganga
You can also enjoy a scenic boat ride on the Krishna River (on a direct payment basis).
Lastly, we’ll drop you off at the Hyderabad railway station or airport. And if time permits, we’ll also make a stop at the
Statue of Equality
(monument dedicated to Shree Ramanujacharya), which is quite close to the Hyderabad Airport.
Hope you enjoyed your trip with us!
Note:
To book your Pooja, Abhishekam, Seva, and more, visit the link:-
https://www.srisailadevasthanam.org/en-in/devotee-app/online-booking/pratyaksha-seva
.
Note:
Statue of Equality is closed on Wednesdays. The entry tickets are as follows:
Adults - Rs. 200/-
Child - Rs. 125/-
Places You’ll See

tamil-nadu-pondicherry-tour.overview:
As you begin the Tamil Nadu and Pondicherry Tour you’ll feel the magic of South India - simple, with welcoming people and full of hidden beauty. See More

The tour starts at Mahabalipuram, popular for its old temples and historical monuments, which is very different from other historical places. Every site has something unique to explore!
Pondicherry is another highlight. If time allows visit French-theme cafes that have a peaceful and luxurious vibe, a perfect spot for sipping coffee. Don't miss Auroville Matrimandir, which looks like a big golden ball where people meditate in silence. There is no puja or mantra, only peace and silence.
Rameshwaram is also an important stop, known for the famous Ramanathaswamy Temple, one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva. There are many hidden gems that people often miss without guidance. Our Tamil Nadu Pondicherry package covers everything for a smooth experience. Just plan your trip with us and enjoy hassle free journey!
See Less

highlights: Explore ancient temples and UNESCO heritage sites in Mahabalipuram, Thanjavur, Chidambaram and Kumbakonam.
Enjoy Pondicherry’s French Quarter, Auroville, cafes and peaceful ashrams.
Visit Rameshwaram with Ramanathaswamy Temple, holy dips, and Rama Setu/Adam’s Bridge.
See Madurai and Tiruchirappalli temples, Rockfort views, museums and local culture.
Experience Kanyakumari sunrise and sunset, Samudra Snanam and meeting point of three oceans.
See More

itinerary.title: Day 1: Arrive Chennai - Mahabalipuram - Pondicherry (160-170km/4-5 hours)
itinerary.description:
Start your
Tamil Nadu and Pondicherry trip
with a pick-up from your selected location in Chennai airport or railway station. Our driver will come to receive you and then you will continue the tour of Mahabalipuram. If you choose a guide, they will travel with the driver and help you on the journey.
After pick-up you will start your tour and visit-
Krishna Mandapam
- This is a rock-cut temple made from a single rock. It has beautiful pictures that shows the stories of Lord Krishna and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Arjuna’s Penance
Cave Temples
- Around 1,300 years old, these caves are peaceful and have stunning rock art – perfect spot for photography.
Pancha Rathas
After covering the main sightseeing in Mahabalipuram, you will drive to Pondicherry. On arrival, check into the hotel. Overnight stay at Pondicherry.
Note-
Krishna Mandapam is open every day from 7 AM to 6 PM.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: DAY 2: Pondicherry - Chidambaram - Kumbakonam (Approx. 133 km / 2.5 Hours)
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out of the hotel and go to the
Auroville Matrimandir
, a calm place for meditation. The Matrimandir and its surrounding gardens have a stunning view, great spot for photography.
Then, drive to the hotel and check in. Next, visit
Sri Aurobindo Ashram
one of India’s most famous ashram. Around 1,200 people live here in its calm spiritual community.
Afterward, visit
Arulmigu Manakula Vinayagar Temple
, an ancient temple dedicated to Lord Ganesh.
Visit the
Puducherry Museum
, famous for its 81 Chola metal statues, one of the largest collections in India.
Later proceed to
Chidambaram
, a temple town famous for the
Thillai Nataraja Temple.
The temple, spread over 40 acres is dedicated to Lord Shiva as Nataraja.
Explore
Gangaikonda Cholapuram
, popular for the
Brihadeeswarar Temple.
This UNESCO World Heritage Site has one of the largest Shiva Lingas, 13 feet tall, with excellent architecture (perfect place for photos ).
Finally drive to
Kumbakonam.
After arriving, check into the hotel for an overnight stay.
Note-
Puducherry Museum is closed on Mondays and holidays.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: DAY 3: Kumbakonam - Thanjavur (Tanjore) - Tiruchirappalli (Trichy) (150 km/ 3.5-4 Hours)
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out and visit
Kumbakonam
, a city filled with unique temples. On arrival, start exploring the sights.
See the
Adi Kumbeswarar Temple.
Nearby is a large temple tank called
Mahamaham Tank
, where devotees take holy dips.
Next travel to
Darasuram
, a small town near
Kumbakonam
, to visit
Airavatesvara Temple.
Later drive to
Thanjavur
(Tanjore). On arrival, visit the
Brihadeeswara Temple
that was built entirely without using any iron or cement.
Then, explore
Thanjavur Palace
where the
Maratha rulers
lived between 1674 and 1855.
Next go to
Thanjavur Art Gallery
filled with beautiful metal and stone art. These works show the rich culture of Tamil history – perfect for art lovers..
After sightseeing proceed to
Tiruchirappalli (Trichy)
. Arrive, check into hotel and stay overnight.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: DAY 4: Tiruchirappalli (Trichy) - Madurai (Approx. 123 km/ 4-5 Hours)
itinerary.description:
Morning after breakfast, check out the hotel and proceed for sightseeing at
Tiruchirappalli.
First, visit
Sri Ranganatha Swamy Temple
, which is one of the 108 Divya Desams (holy shrines of Vishnu).
Then proceed to the
Jambukeswarar Akilandeswari Temple
where water from a small underground flow falls on the Shiva Lingam - something truly special.
After that, visit
Ucchi Pillayar
Temple, dedicated to Lord Ganesha, located on
Rockfort
, with stunning city views from the top ( don’t forget to take photos ).
Then visit the
Government Museum
at Rani Mangammal Mahal, where you can see collections of art, history and local wildlife.
After that visit the
Butterfly Park
to see colorful butterflies, and explore Nakshatra Vanam, which has 27 trees linked to stars and zodiac signs in Indian astrology.
After sightseeing, proceed to
Madurai.
On arrival, check in to the hotel and enjoy an overnight stay.
Note-
Government Museum timings are 10 AM to 5 PM.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: DAY 5: Madurai - Rameshwaram (173 km/ 3-4 Hours)
itinerary.description:
On the fifth day of your
trip
, have breakfast, check out of the hotel, and start your sightseeing tour of
Madurai.
Visit
Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple
, a beautiful old temple near the
Vaigai River
(looks stunning in the evening due to lights).
Then, see
Thiruparankundram Murugan Temple.
Later, drive to
Rameshwaram
, located on
Pamban Island.
According to mythology, Rama made a bridge here to reach Lanka and rescue Sita from Ravana.
On arrival, check into your hotel. Then explore
Ramanathaswamy Temple, Agnitheertham, and Ramjharoka Temple.
Stay overnight in Rameshwaram.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: DAY 6: In Rameswaram
itinerary.description:
Early in the morning, around
5:00 AM
, proceed to the
Spatika Linga Darshan
, also called
Mani Darshan
, where the natural crystal Shivling (not man-made) is very important in Hinduism and looks very beautiful.
Later you will head out for
Agni Teertham
to have a holy bath in the sea.
Further proceed to the main temple through North gate and
Take sacred bath with holy water of the 22 wells, inside the
Ramanathaswamy Temple
during
Theerth Snanam.
Then proceed for darshan and pooja at the main temple.
After checking out of the hotel, proceed to visit
Five-faced Hanuman Temple.
Next, explore
Ramar Patham
and
Kothandaramaswamy Temple, Rama Setu/ Adam’s Bridge
(stones placed by Lord Rama that don’t sink), and visit
Gandamadana Parvatham
, where Lord
Rama’s footprint
is believed to be.
Also, explore
A. P. J. Abdul Kalam’s house
, the home of India’s famous scientist and former President.
Go to
Dhanushkodi
, an old town at Rameshwaram Island. If time allows, explore and enjoy the beaches.
On arrival, check into the hotel. Overnight stay in
Rameshwaram.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: DAY 7: Rameswaram - Kanyakumari (312 kms/ 7 Hours)
itinerary.description:
In the morning, visit the temple once again or take a
Samudra Snanam
(holy dip in the sea). Afterward, check out of the hotel and drive to
Kanyakumari
, the point where the Bay of Bengal, the Arabian Sea, and the Indian Ocean meet.
Kanyakumari
is famous for being the only place where you can see both the sunrise and sunset over the ocean.
On arrival, check into your hotel and relax for the rest of the day. Stay overnight at the hotel.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: DAY 8: Kanyakumari - Kovalam - Thiruvananthapuram (Trivandrum) (Approx. 109/ 3 Hrs)
itinerary.description:
Early in the morning, you can watch the beautiful
sunrise in Kanyakumari.
The calm atmosphere makes it a perfect time to take pictures.
Later return to hotel for breakfast.
After breakfast visit the
Swami Vivekananda Rock Memorial
- a quiet place surrounded by the sea. Walk over the Sea by Glass bridge to reach Thiruvalluvar Statue.
If you have time, take a boat ride.
Next move to the famous
Kanyakumari Temple
, also known as
Kumari Amman Temple.
This temple is built in
Kerala-style architecture
, so just get ready to click photos.
You can also visit
Triveni Sangam
where the three oceans meet, and
Gandhi Mandapam
, built at the place where Mahatma Gandhi’s ashes were kept before being put into the sea.
Don’t miss the impressive
Thiruvalluvar Statue
built in memory of the great Tamil poet and philosopher.
Later drive towards
Trivandrum.
On the way visit
Thanumalayan Temple
at
Suchindram
famous for its beautiful architecture and the 22-foot-tall statue of Lord Hanuman.
Then continue to
Padmanabhapuram Palace
known for its traditional
Kerala
-style design. Don’t forget to take some photos.
If time permits stop at
Kovalam Beach
for a short visit before heading to Trivandrum.
On arrival, check into the hotel and later visit
Sri Padmanabhaswamy Temple
dedicated to Lord Vishnu.
Overnight stay at Trivandrum.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: DAY 9: Thiruvananthapuram (Trivandrum) (Departure)
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, your
trip to Pondicherry and Tamil Nadu
ends with happy memories as you are transferred to Trivandrum Airport or railway station for your onward journey.

tamilnadu-pilgrimage-tour.overview:
Do you believe South India is only famous for temples? See More

This Tamil Nadu pilgrimage tour Package will surprise you with its mix of heritage, seaside beauty, and rich culture. From Chennai, the trip takes you first to Mahabalipuram, famous for the Pancha Rathas, where each temple is made from a single big stone.
In Rameswaram, you can see Ram Setu, a line of stones in the sea. Some of them even float! People believe Lord Rama built this bridge to reach Lanka and save Sita. You will also visit Ooty. Be sure to see its popular Botanical Garden, full of rare, colorful flowers and excellent surroundings - it’s truly memorable for nature lovers.
The trip also covers Kanchipuram, famous for its silk Sarees. Make sure to shop if you get the chance. There’s much more to explore! Just get ready to discover such
hidden gems waiting for you on this Tamil Nadu pilgrimage tour Plan.
See Less

highlights: Explore famous temples, heritage sites, and unique architecture across Tamil Nadu.
Spend time near the sea, enjoy hills and see beautiful gardens at Ooty and Kodaikanal.
Explore cultural spots like Kanchipuram for silk shopping and Pondicherry for peaceful experiences.
Visit famous places such as Rama Setu, Brihadeeswarar Temple and Annamalaiyar Temple.
See More

itinerary.title: Day 1: Arrival Chennai - Mahabalipuram - Pondicherry (250 - 280 km/ 6 - 7 hours)
itinerary.description:
Start your Tamil Nadu trip. Your journey begins in Chennai, where our
My Quick Trippers
team will meet you at Chennai Railway Station or airport and take you to Mahabalipuram to see the main sights. Later, continue to Pondicherry for local sightseeing. If you have a guide, they will join the driver and help you for the whole day.
Explore These Places in Mahabalipuram
Five Rathas-
ancient rock-cut temples, the best destination to click photos.
Cave Temple-
A beautiful temple around
1,200–1,300 years old.
Arjuna’s Penance-
In Mahabalipuram, a huge rock shows a story from the Mahabharata. Arjuna is shown meditating to gain special powers surrounded by gods, animals and magical scenes.
In Pondicherry, you will visit-
Artificial Beach-
A man-made seaside spot.
Auroville Ashram-
It is a peaceful community where people from around the world live together. Many visitors come here from far away to experience its unique meditation.
Once sightseeing is done, spend the night in Pondicherry.
Note-
Carry water, sun protection, and comfortable walking shoes. Photography is allowed at most places, but follow local rules.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 2: Pondicherry- Chidambaram- Kumbakonam (140 km/3-4 hours)
itinerary.description:
In the morning, go to Chidambaram and spend time at the Nataraja Temple. This temple covers an area of 40 acres. It is famous for its unique architecture and is perfect for taking pictures.
Later, drive to
Kumbakonam
. On arrival, in
Kumbakonam, visit Oppiliappan Koil, Thiruvenkadu,Thirunageswaram
(oldest temple around 1,100 years),
Thirumanancheri
(known for beautiful surroundings),
Patteeswaram
,
Alangudi
,
Suriyanar Kovil
(best for morning sunrise views),
Kanjanur
,
Vaitheeswaran Temple
,
Keezhaperumpallam
,
Thingalur
,
Thirunallar
.
Overnight stay at the hotel.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 3: Kumbakonam-Tanjore -Trichy (95 - 100 km/2.5 -3 hours)
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, visit
Tanjore
to see the
Brihadeeswarar Temple
, famous for one of the largest Shiva lingams in India. Next, explore
Tanjore Palace
and its
museum
.
Later, travel to
Trichy
. See the
Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple
in
Srirangam
, visit
Rockfort
(best place to click photos from the top because of city views), then also visit
Samayapura
, and
Thiruvanaikaval
.
After having dinner, continue to
Rameswaram
and stay overnight there.
Note-
Brihadeeswarar Temple timing is
6am -12:30pm
,
4pm - 8:30pm
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 4: Trichy - Rameswaram (228 Kms/ 6-7 hours)
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, travel to Rameswaram.
Enjoy sightseeing in
Rameswaram
and visit
Pamban Bridge
(famous sea bridge with amazing views),
Ramanatha Swamy Temple
,
Ramar Patham
(believed footprints of Lord Rama),
Kothandaramaswamy Temple
,
Agni Theertham
(holy water for ritual baths),
Dhanushkodi
(scenic beaches to click photos),
Hanuman Temple
and
floating stonenear Hanuman ji temple
(sacred stone that floats on water called Ram Setu).
Then, return to the hotel, enjoy dinner, and stay overnight.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 5: Rameshwaram - Madurai - Kodaikanal (Distance approx, 313 km/ 6-7 hours)
itinerary.description:
Early in the morning, start with
Spatika Lingam Darshan
at the
Ramanathaswamy Temple
in
Rameswaram
. After that, proceed to
Madurai
. Visit the
Meenakshi Amman Temple
and enjoy its stunning design. This temple has
14 colorful towers
, which makes it more unique than many other temples.
After sightseeing in
Madurai
, drive to
Kodaikanal
. On arrival, check into the hotel. Overnight stay at Kodaikanal.
Note-
Meenakshi Amman Temple is closed during lunch hours (around
12:00pm
-
4:30pm
), so plan your visit accordingly.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 6: Kodaikanal Sightseeing
itinerary.description:
After breakfast start sightseeing in
Kodaikanal
. Enjoy beautiful hills and fresh mountain air.
In
Kodaikanal
, visit
Bryant Park
(a beautiful garden with colorful flowers),
Coakers Walk
,
Pillar Rock
,
Suicide Point
(breathtaking views of valleys and forests for photos),
Silver Falls
(180 feet waterfall hidden in the forest),
Bear Shola Falls
,
Kurinji Andavar Temple
(special Kurinji flowers bloom here once every 12 years) and
Kodaikanal Lake
( perfect for boating and relaxing ).
Return to the hotel for relaxation after a day full of sightseeing. Overnight stay at
Kodaikanal
.
Note-
Kodaikanal is at a high altitude, so the weather can be cool even during the day. Carry warm clothes.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 7: Kodaikanal - Palani - Ooty
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, drive to
Ooty
. Stop at
Palani
to visit the
Murugan Temple
(famous for its 600+ stairs going up the hill) and visit Coonoor to enjoy the beautiful tea gardens and hill views.
After arriving in
Ooty
, check into the hotel.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 8: Ooty - Tiruvannamala
itinerary.description:
After breakfast proceed for Ooty sightseeing. Explore the key attractions and enjoy the natural beauty of this hill station.
In Ooty, visit
Botanical Gardens
,
Rose Garden
(India’s largest with 2,000+ rose varieties),
Ooty Lake
(boating and horse rides),
Doddabetta Peak
(known for the highest Nilgiri peak with valley views),
Government Museum
,
Pykara Falls
(scenic waterfall for photography),
Chocolate Factory
,
Golf Course
and
Lady Canning’s Seat
.
Have dinner after sightseeing and continue your night journey to
Tiruvannamalai
.
Note-
Since it’s a hilly area, download maps before you start.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 9: Tiruvannamalai Sightseeing
itinerary.description:
Check into the hotel in
Tiruvannamalai
. After that, proceed for sightseeing. Have Darshan of Lord Annamalaiyar at the famous
Annamalaiyar Temple
. Unlike most temples, Annamalaiyar Temple has a special ritual called Girivalam, where devotees walk around the Arunachala Hill at night on full moon days for spiritual blessings.
Overnight stay at the hotel in
Tiruvannamalai
.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 10: Tiruvannamalai - Kanchipuram - Thiruttani (Approx. 195 km/ 5.5 hours )
itinerary.description:
Start your day with a road trip to
Kanchipuram
. Once you arrive visit the famous
Ekambareswarar Temple

itinerary.title: DAY 01: Arrival - Chennai - Tirupati (3 hrs/140 kms)
itinerary.description:
Arrive at Chennai and meet our representative at Chennai Railway Station/Airport.
Our representative will make all the arrangements to transfer you to Tirupati, which is dotted with cultural and historical treasures.
This is a famous pilgrimage town in Andhra Pradesh, home to the Vaishnavite shrine of Tirumala Venkateswara Temple.
After reaching Tirupati, you will check into your hotel and relax for some time.
You will then head to the Tirumala Hills, that is known to be the sacred abode of Lord Venkateshwara.
The Tirumala hills are a group of seven peaks, namely Anjanadri, Vrushabadri, Narayanadri, Seshadri, Neeladri, Garudadri, and Venkatadri.
Please Note:-
Without a darshan ticket, you won't be able to have darshan at Tirupati. You can opt for Sarva Darshanam.
You can choose from two options. Without or with a token, Sarva Darshanam will take more time for darshan. 12-18 hours on weekends, 8-12 hours on regular days, and 12-36 hours on festival days.
Without a Darshan Ticket, you may be able to visit Tirumala, but you won't be able to have Darshan at the Main Temple.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 02: Tirupati Darshan-(3 Hrs/110 Kms)- Vellore -(2Hrs/95 Kms)-Tiruvannamalai
itinerary.description:
Have a delicious breakfast in the morning, and then you will head to Kanipakam and Srinivasa Mangapuram.
Later, you will head to Vellore, which houses the Golden Temple.
After arriving at Vellore, you will visit the Golden Temple that is situated at Sripuram and built in honor of goddess Lakshmi. The temple's architecture is star-shaped, and the goddess has been placed in the middle of the star.
Then you will head to Tiruvannamalai, a renowned pilgrimage center situated at the foothills of Annamalai hills.
Once you have arrived, you will check into your pre-booked hotel and visit the main temple. Tiruvannamalai houses Annamalaiyar Temple, which is dedicated to Shiva and worshiped as Annamalaiyar or Arunachalesvara. It is one of the largest temples in India that houses four gateway towers. The Shiva Lingam here has an association with the Pancha Bhoota, specifically the element of Fire.
After the darshan, you will head back to your hotel and have an overnight stay.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 03: Tiruvannamalai - (220 Kms/ 5 Hrs)- Thanjavur (Tanjore) - (75 Kms/ 2 Hrs)-Tiruchirappalli (Trichy)
itinerary.description:
Relish a delicious breakfast in the morning, and then you will check out of your hotel and get ready for sightseeing in Thanjavur.
You will visit the famous attractions, including the Brihadeeswara Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the biggest temple in the region. This architectural marvel was built by Raja Raja Chola during the 11th century.
You will then visit Thanjavur Palace, a historical structure in Thanjavur. It was the Maratha rulers' official residence from 1674 to 1855.
Then you will visit the Thanjavur Art Gallery, where you will see a treasured collection of stone sculptures, bronze icons, and other artifacts, which testify to the golden age in Tamil history.
You will then embark on a drive to Tiruchirappalli, renowned for its historical attractions.
After arriving in Tiruchirappalli, you will check into your hotel and have an overnight stay.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 04: Tiruchirappalli - Madurai- (3 hrs/140 km)
itinerary.description:
Relish a tasty breakfast in the morning, and then you will check out of your hotel.
You will get ready for a sightseeing tour of Tiruchirapalli.
You will visit the Sri Ranganatha Swamy temple, which is dedicated to Lord Ranganatha Swamy and is considered to be the most important of the one hundred and eight main Vishnu temples.
You will then visit the Jambukeswarar Akilandeswari Temple, which is built in honor of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvathi. The temple has an association with the Pancha Bhoota, specifically the element of Water (Jala).
Then you will get ready to visit Ucchi Pillayar Temple. This seventh-century Hindu temple is situated at the top of Rockfort and is dedicated to Lord Ganesha.
You will also visit the Government Museum, which is located in Bharathidasan San town at Rani Mangammal Mahal. The museum comprises a wide range of exhibits related to anthropology, epigraphy, geology, zoology, paintings, and history.
You will then head to Tropical Butterfly Conservatory Campus, the Tropical Butterfly Conservatory. Then you will drive to Madurai.
After arriving at Madurai, you will check into your hotel and have an overnight stay.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 05: Madurai - Rameshwaram (3 hrs/180 km)
itinerary.description:
Post breakfast, you will check out of the hotel and head out for a sightseeing tour of Madurai.
You will visit the famous attractions such as the Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple, which is situated on the southern banks of the river Vaigai. The complex has twelve gateway towers, ranging in height from 45-50 m.
Then you will head to Thiruparankundram Murugan Temple, one of the six abodes of Lord Murugan.
You will then head to Rameshwaram, which is situated on Pamban Island and is separated by the Pamban channel from mainland India. According to legend, Rameshwaram is considered to be the spot from where Rama built a bridge to rescue his consort Sita from Ravana.
You will then head to Rameshwaram and check into your hotel.
You will then visit Ramanathaswamy Temple, Ramjharoka Temple, and Agnitheertham and have an overnight stay at your hotel in Rameshwaram.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 06: Rameswaram - Kanyakumari - (6 hrs/310 km)
itinerary.description:
Early morning, you will take a dip in the sacred water of Agni Theertham, and then you will go for Sphatik Lingam Darshan.
After the darshan and holy bath, you will head back to your hotel and have a tasty breakfast.
You will then head out for a sightseeing tour of Rameshwaram, which includes Ramar Patham, Five-faced Hanuman Temple, Gandamadana Parvatham/ Lord Rama footprint, Kothandaramaswamy Temple, Former President A. P. J. Abdul Kalam House, Rama Setu/ Adam's Bridge, and Dhanushkodi.
You will then head to Kanyakumari -the Indian Peninsula's southernmost point and the confluence of three oceans - the Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal, and the Indian Ocean.
After arriving at Kanyakumari, you will check into your hotel and have an overnight stay.
Dhanushkodi:
Adam's Bridge is the main attraction of Dhanushkodi. You can reach this place by hiring a jeep (4-wheel drive). It is a tip of the island where normal cars don't go.
Kothandaraman Temple:
This is the sacred site where Vibhishana surrendered to Lord Rama. In this temple, Rama, the main idol, has been depicted with a bow and arrow.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 07: Kanyakumari - Kovalam - Thiruvananthapuram (Trivandrum) (2 Hrs/100 Kms)
itinerary.description:
Early in the morning, you will head out for a sunrise view in Kanyakumari.
You will then head back to your hotel and have a Scrumptious breakfast.
You will then head out to visit the Swami Vivekananda Rock Memorial, the meditation hall, and the Smarak. You will then head to Kanyakumari mandir, one of the 51 Shakti Peethas.
Other attractions that you will visit include Gandhi Mandapam, which has been built on the place where the urn containing the ashes of Mahatma Gandhi was kept before immersion for public viewing.
You will also see the Thiruvalluvar Statue, and then you will drive to Trivandrum.
On the way to "Suchindram", you will visit the Thanumalayan temple, known for its splendid architecture. Later, you will visit the "Padmanabhapuram Palace," a sixteenth-century wooden palace where the Travancore king resided.
If you have time, you can visit Kovalam beach, and then you will head to Trivandrum.
After arriving at Trivandrum, you will check into your hotel.
After relaxing for some time, you will visit the Sri Padmanabhaswamy temple, which is dedicated to Visnu/Krishna.
You will then have an overnight stay at your hotel in Trivandrum.
Places You’ll See

itinerary.title: Day 08: Thiruvananthapuram (Trivandrum) (Departure)
itinerary.description:
Savour a lip-smacking breakfast, and then you will check out of your hotel.
You will be transferred to Trivandrum railway station or the Airport from where you will continue your journey to your hometown.
Places You’ll See

Ready to explore a state full of rich history and colorful culture? The Varanasi Prayagraj Ayodhya Naimisharanya Tour lets you experience it all. See More

Start with Varanasi, India’s oldest city, with over 80 Ghats that attract many tourists. Besides temples and Ghats not many people know that this holy place is also used for TV shoots because of its beautiful surroundings. Don’t miss a boat ride on the Ganga for unforgettable memories.
Now the journey continues to Prayagraj, where you will visit the famous Prayagraj Fort near the Yamuna River, built by Mughal King Akbar. One interesting thing is the underground Patalpuri Temple in the fort, which few people can visit. Next, the tour moves to Ayodhya, the birthplace of Lord Rama. The special thing about Ram Ji’s temple is that, even without cement or iron, it is strong. Every person gets inner peace here.
Finally, the journey ends in Lucknow, the city of Nawabs. Visit the Bada Imambara famous for its beautiful architecture and the thrilling Bhool Bhulaiyaa maze inside. There is a lot to explore; just plan your Varanasi Prayagraj Ayodhya Naimisharanya trip for a better experience.

Our Varanasi Bodhgaya Prayagraj Tour Package gives you a complete experience of both cities. First, we will explore Varanasi, known for its colorful and attractive culture that people from different countries specially come here to see its beautiful temples, old traditions, local music, Ghats, and the peaceful Ganges River.

During Buddha Jayanti, visitors can enjoy unique activities and colorful celebrations at the Mahabodhi Temple, which you shouldn't miss! Get ready for Varanasi to Bodhgaya Prayagraj tour!

The Yamuna Pushkaralu Tour from Delhi is a 4 Days / 3 Nights trip. See More

It is designed for pilgrims who want to seek the blessing of the goddess Yamuna on the auspicious event of Pushkaralu which takes place only once every 12 years. It is marked by the special astrological event when Jupiter enters Cancer. This holy tour will take you to the revered Yamunotri Temple from Delhi via Haridwar, Dehradun, Mussoorie, Barkot, and Janki Chatti.
Significance
It is believed that attending this special event and performing rituals cleanses sins and removes negative karmas. In addition, it grants relief from Pitru Dosha and other planetary afflictions. Pilgrims who come here perform the holy rituals such as Pushkara Snanam, ancestral rituals, and special pujas.
This tour brings together spirituality with natural beauty – giving you a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for memorable experiences.
See Less

itinerary.title: Day 01: Arrival at Dehradun and Local Sightseeing
itinerary.description:
You begin your journey by arriving at
Dehradun Airport or Railway Station
, where a tour representative receives you and helps with the transfer. The drive itself is short, but traffic around Dehradun and Haridwar can sometimes slow things down, especially during pilgrimage seasons.
After checking into your
pre-booked hotel
, it’s advisable to rest for a while. The terrain and climate here are different from the plains, and even light travel fatigue can show up early.
Later in the day, you visit two well-known local attractions:
Robber’s Cave, a narrow river cave that requires a short walk on uneven ground
Tapkeshwar Temple, a naturally formed cave temple where water continuously drips over the Shivling
Both places are popular, so expect crowds in the afternoon. Comfortable footwear is important here.
The evening is kept light. You return to the hotel and settle in for an overnight stay, allowing your body to adjust before the next day’s rituals.

itinerary.title: Day 02: Dakpatthar Visit and Yamuna Pushkaralu Rituals
itinerary.description:
This is the most spiritually significant day of the tour and also the most physically engaging.
After an early start, you drive towards
Dakpatthar
, a quiet stretch along the River Yamuna. The area is calmer than Haridwar, but during Yamuna Pushkaralu, the ghats can still become crowded at peak ritual hours.
Here, you take a holy dip in the Yamuna, followed by participation in the
Yamuna Pushkaralu
rituals. These rituals often take time, depending on priest availability and crowd flow, so patience is important. Elderly travellers or those with mobility concerns should move cautiously, as river steps can be slippery.
Post rituals, you return to Haridwar by afternoon.
In the evening, the focus shifts to the River Ganga:
A sacred dip at
Har Ki Pauri
, where crowd density is usually high
Attendance at the evening
Ganga Aarti
, which is spiritually uplifting but involves standing for a long duration
A visit to
Brahma Kund
, traditionally believed to be the spot where drops of Amrit fell
After a long but fulfilling day, you return to the hotel for a
quiet overnight stay
.

Dehradun Airport or the railway station
, depending on your onward journey. Morning departures are usually smoother, while afternoon travel may face traffic near Haridwar.
With this, the
Yamuna Pushkaralu 2026 journey concludes

yamuna-pushkaralu-yatra-to-kashi-ayodhya.overview:
The Yamuna Pushkaralu Spiritual Tour offers you a trip of divine purification during the auspicious Yamuna Pushkaram. See More

This event falls only once in 12 years, when Jupiter enters Cancer. Enjoy this spiritual journey with visits to the eternally holy cities of Varanasi, Prayagraj, and Ayodhya. You’ll also be visiting the ‘City of Tehzeeb’ – Lucknow.
On this tour, you’ll be performing ancestral rituals (Pitru Tarpan & Pinda Pradan), visiting temples, taking holy dips, and witnessing river Aarti. All in all, this journey blends faith and tradition – all in a span of four days!
Spiritual Significance of Yamuna Pushkaralu
It is believed that during the 12-day period of Yamuna Pushkaralu, Goddess Yamuna grants special boon to her devotees. In addition, taking holy dips in this period is said to cleanse the sins of past lives and purifies negative karmas. You also get freed from Pitru Dosha, Naga Dosha, and planetary afflictions.
Overall, this tour brings spiritual upliftment to devotees as well as peace to their ancestors.

itinerary.title: Day 2: Varanasi – Prayagraj (130 kms / 4 Hrs)
itinerary.description:
In the morning, you’ll be driven to Prayagraj.
On arrival, check into your hotel.
Later, you’ll be taken to the Triveni Sangam – confluence of Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati rivers. Take a holy dip here and perform other sacred rituals.
After this, take a boat ride in Sangam.
Now, you’ll be taken to the following places:
Bade Hanuman Mandir:
Seek Darshan of Lord Hanuman.
Akshayavat Temple and Tree:
This sacred fig tree is believed to be the one under which Ram, Lakshman, and Sita rested. As per the ancient Hindu texts, it’s believed that whoever worships Akshayavat gets freed from sins.
Prayagraj Fort (Allahabad Fort):
This was built by Akbar in 1583. Its vicinity to the sacred Yamuna River gives it a spiritual touch.
Alopi Devi Temple:
This is also a Shaktipith temple.
Lalita Devi Temple:
It is revered as Madhaveswari Devi in scriptures. It is believed that the fingers of Maa Sati’s hand fell here.
Shri Nagvasuki Temple:
Devotees believe that worshipping here removes obstacles, protects from snake afflictions (Sarpa Dosh), and brings peace and prosperity.
Your overnight stay will be in Prayagraj.

Kanak Bhavan Temple:
It’s known for its gold-plated domes.
Ram ki Paidi:
This is yet another temple dedicated to Lord Rama.
Dashrath Mahal:
This was the residence of Lord Ram's father, King Dashrath.
In the evening, you’ll be taken to attend the Saryu River Aarti at Naya Ghat. Also, take this time to stroll around the Saryu River banks.
Your overnight stay will be in Ayodhya.

itinerary.description:
In the early morning, you’ll be driven to Jankichatti – the starting point of the trek.
Once you get there, trek to Yamunotri (6 km). You can do that either by foot or take the service of pony/Doli (on a direct payment basis).
Take a holy dip in the waters of River Yamuna. This is especially auspicious during Yamuna Pushkar.
At Surya Kund, cook rice in the hot spring and take this home as Prasadam.
At Divya Shila, offer your prayers and seek blessings of Mata Yamuna.
Once you reach the Yamunotri temple, complete your Darshan and Poojan. Goddess Yamuna is believed to be daughter of Lord Surya and sister of Yamraj.
Trek back to Jankichatti.
